nodes.name: checkRateLimit
nodes.summary: Applies the shared token-bucket limiter to a request/route/user combination and returns a 429 JSON response with Retry-After when exhausted, or null to proceed.

nodes.name: createMemoryBus
nodes.summary: Factory for the in-memory bus adapter: publish delivers synchronously to topic subscribers, subscribe returns an unsubscribe closure, and close clears all subscriptions.

nodes.name: createPgBus
nodes.summary: Factory for the Postgres-backed bus: maintains a dedicated LISTEN connection with exponential-backoff reconnects, relays incoming NOTIFY payloads to the local memory bus, and broadcasts publishes via NOTIFY while ignoring self-originated messages.

nodes.name: getBus
nodes.summary: Returns the process-wide bus instance, lazily constructing a Postgres adapter when DATABASE_URL is set (logging a warning and falling back to the memory adapter on failure).

nodes.name: _resetBusForTests
nodes.summary: Test-only helper that closes and discards the current bus singleton so a fresh adapter is created on next access.

nodes.name: createPresenceRegistry
nodes.summary: Factory for a presence registry with connection reference counting per user, heartbeat refresh, stale-entry sweep returning dropped users, and online-state queries.

nodes.name: getPresence
nodes.summary: Returns the process-wide presence registry singleton, creating it on first access.

nodes.name: parseTopic
nodes.summary: Splits a topic string at its first separator into its kind and identifier parts, returning null for malformed topics.

nodes.name: export-org.mjs
nodes.summary: CLI runner for the per-tenant cutover export: builds DMMF-derived model plans, collects one org's rows plus referential closure via the shared export core, and writes one NDJSON file per table plus a manifest.json with counts, columns, and type categories.
nodes.languageNotes: An .mjs script run under tsx so it can import the TypeScript lib modules directly.

nodes.name: import-org.mjs
nodes.summary: CLI runner for the per-tenant idempotent import/replay: reads the NDJSON export directory and manifest, then loads all tables in one owner transaction under session_replication_role=replica via the shared import core (append-only DO NOTHING, mutable last-writer-wins UPSERT).

nodes.name: export-core.ts
nodes.summary: Shared export collection engine used by both the full export and the soak-sync delta replay: runs strict org-scoped SELECTs (optionally narrowed by watermark delta filters) plus the two-phase referential closure inside one REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY snapshot, returning per-table encoded rows, type categories, and observed watermarks.
nodes.languageNotes: Delta filters are ANDed onto the org-scope WHERE clause so an incremental export can only narrow, never widen, tenant scope.

nodes.name: import-core.ts
nodes.summary: Shared idempotent-import engine: one owner transaction with SET LOCAL session_replication_role=replica, per-row UPSERTs in plan order, DataClassification dedupe-with-audit, and an in-transaction orphan probe that rolls back the whole load on any dangling FK.

nodes.name: model-graph.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the DMMF-derived migration plan: verifies model inclusion/exclusion lists, org-scope path resolution, append-only classification, scoped SELECT SQL, FK edge derivation, delete-eligibility guards, and delete ordering against a fake pg client.

nodes.name: model-graph.ts
nodes.summary: The schema-driven migration plan for the cutover engine: derives at runtime from the Prisma DMMF and live information_schema which models move and how — table/PK/org-scope path (DIRECT/PARENT/ROOT/MEMBER), append-only vs mutable, money columns, stripped generated columns, FK edges for referential closure, orphan probes, and children-before-parents delete ordering.
nodes.languageNotes: Nothing is hardcoded: the Prisma DMMF is the single source of truth, so adding or renaming a model cannot silently rot the migration plan.

nodes.name: ndjson-codec.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the lossless NDJSON row codec: Date/Buffer envelope round-trips, category-driven decoding by PG type OID, and the jsonBindParam wrapper that keeps jsonb array values valid on import bind.

nodes.name: ndjson-codec.ts
nodes.summary: Lossless, type-aware row codec for the export NDJSON: wraps only Date and Buffer in tagged envelopes, classifies columns by PG type OID (bytea/timestamp/json/passthrough), and decodes by recorded category rather than value-sniffing so jsonb data can never collide with the envelope format.
nodes.languageNotes: jsonBindParam wraps json/jsonb values with a toPostgres hook so node-postgres serializes JS arrays as JSON instead of Postgres array literals.

nodes.name: pg-utc.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the UTC timestamp fix: asserts the OID-1114 parser returns UTC ISO strings regardless of host timezone and that the watermark round-trip through model-graph and watermark helpers is offset-free.

nodes.name: pg-utc.ts
nodes.summary: Timezone-correct watermark round-trip fix: forces process.env.TZ to UTC and registers a node-pg parser for OID 1114 (timestamp without time zone) that interprets stored wall-clock values as UTC, so delta watermarks can never silently skip rows on hosts west of UTC.
nodes.languageNotes: Must run before any Date or pg use — Node caches $TZ on first Date construction, so a late set is a no-op.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full export: validates CLI args and org UUID, connects to the source, filters model plans to tables that exist in the live source, collects org rows plus closure, then writes per-table NDJSON files and a manifest.json with counts and type categories.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the full import: reads manifest.json and per-table NDJSON files into import units, connects to the target as DB owner, runs the single-transaction idempotent load, and prints per-table inserted/updated/skipped totals.

nodes.name: collectOrgRows
nodes.summary: Collects one org's rows for all planned tables in a REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY snapshot: Phase 1 runs the strict org-scope SELECT (optionally narrowed by delta filters) capturing type categories and observed watermarks; Phase 2 pulls FK-referenced parent rows (global built-ins, shared users) so the set is referentially complete.

nodes.name: importUnits
nodes.summary: Loads table import units in one owner transaction under session_replication_role=replica: dedupes DataClassification rows with audit, executes per-row idempotent UPSERTs counting inserted/updated/skipped, then runs the orphan probe and throws (rolling back) on any dangling FK.

nodes.name: rankOf
nodes.summary: Returns the ordinal rank of a data-classification level in the canonical order, used by the DataClassification dedupe to keep the highest ceiling per org.

nodes.name: dmmfModels
nodes.summary: Loads and memoizes the Prisma DMMF model list by shelling out to a generator helper, providing the single source of truth for the migration plan.

nodes.name: resolveScope
nodes.summary: Determines how a model's rows are tied to one org: DIRECT via an org_id column, PARENT via a breadth-first walk of to-one FK chains to an org-scoped ancestor, ROOT for Organization itself, or MEMBER for User via org membership.

nodes.name: buildModelPlans
nodes.summary: Builds the full ordered list of ModelPlans from the DMMF: skips v2-only and excluded global models, resolves each model's org-scope path, table, PK, mutability, and money columns, and returns plans in FK-safe load order.

nodes.name: orderForLoad
nodes.summary: Sorts model plans into a deterministic load order by scope tier then table name so parents tend to load before children.

nodes.name: modelPlanByName
nodes.summary: Returns a Map of model name to ModelPlan built from buildModelPlans for quick lookup.

nodes.name: resolveColumns
nodes.summary: Intersects a model's DMMF copyable scalar columns with the live database's information_schema columns, stripping GENERATED columns (content_tsv), search_vector, and db-only extras, and reports what was stripped plus whether the PK survived.

nodes.name: buildScopedSelect
nodes.summary: Builds the strict org-scoped SELECT for a plan: direct org_id filter, multi-hop JOIN chains for PARENT scope, id/membership filters for ROOT/MEMBER, an optional ANDed extra filter (watermark delta), and deterministic PK ordering.

nodes.name: quoteIdent
nodes.summary: Safely quotes a SQL identifier, passing simple identifiers through and double-quoting anything else to prevent injection via table or column names.

nodes.name: fkEdgesOf
nodes.summary: Derives a model's outbound FK edges from DMMF to-one relations plus the enumerated bare user-reference columns, giving the referential-closure and delete-ordering logic its dependency graph.

nodes.name: closureTargetTables
nodes.summary: Aggregates the distinct FK target tables reachable from a set of plans, used to decide which parent tables the referential closure must probe.

nodes.name: migratedTableSet
nodes.summary: Returns the set of physical table names covered by the given migration plans.

nodes.name: discoverOrphanProbeTargets
nodes.summary: Discovers every FK constraint among migrated tables from the live pg_constraint catalog (plus DMMF-derived bare user refs) to produce the list of child/parent column pairs the orphan probe must check.

nodes.name: orphanProbeSql
nodes.summary: Builds the dangling-FK probe SQL for one target: counts child rows whose FK value has no matching parent row.

nodes.name: deleteExtrasPlans
nodes.summary: Filters plans down to the tables eligible for delete-extras in the final reconcile: org-owned (DIRECT/PARENT), mutable, and not append-only/audit — everything else is hard-excluded.

nodes.name: deleteForbiddenReason
nodes.summary: Returns a human-readable reason why deleting from a plan's table is forbidden (append-only/audit, non-org-owned scope), or null if deletion is allowed — a per-table fail-closed guard.

nodes.name: orderForDelete
nodes.summary: Computes the children-before-parents delete order for delete-extras: reads live FK constraints, builds a parent→child graph over eligible tables, topologically sorts it (Kahn), warns on cycles, and returns plans in reverse-topological order.

nodes.name: buildScopedPkSelect
nodes.summary: Builds a strict org-scoped SELECT returning only the PK column, used by the reconcile PK-set diff.

nodes.name: categoryForOid
nodes.summary: Classifies a PG type OID into a decode category: bytea, timestamp, json, or passthrough.

nodes.name: jsonBindParam
nodes.summary: Wraps a json/jsonb value in a toPostgres object so node-postgres binds it as JSON text for every shape, preventing JS arrays from being rendered as invalid Postgres array literals.

nodes.name: encodeValue
nodes.summary: Encodes a single pg-driver value for NDJSON: Buffers become base64 envelopes, Dates become ISO envelopes, everything else passes through as native JSON.

nodes.name: decodeValue
nodes.summary: Decodes an NDJSON value by its column's recorded PG type category — unwrapping bytea/timestamp envelopes, wrapping json values for safe binding — never sniffing values, so jsonb data cannot collide with the envelope format.

nodes.name: encodeRow
nodes.summary: Encodes one result row into an NDJSON-safe object by applying encodeValue to each column.

nodes.name: decodeRow
nodes.summary: Decodes one NDJSON row into an ordered bind-parameter array using each column's recorded type category.

nodes.name: forceUtcProcessTz
nodes.summary: Sets process.env.TZ to UTC so JS Date math and toISOString are offset-free; must run before any Date construction.

nodes.name: registerUtcTimestampParser
nodes.summary: Registers a node-pg type parser for OID 1114 that appends Z to the raw timestamp text so timestamp-without-tz values are read as canonical UTC ISO strings on any host timezone.

nodes.name: setupUtcTimestamps
nodes.summary: Convenience entry that applies both UTC fixes — forcing the process timezone and registering the OID-1114 parser — called at the top of every runner script.

nodes.name: reconcile-core.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the delete-extras engine: verifies the pure PK-set diff, delete-plan computation against eligible-table guards, and threshold/fail-closed behavior without a live database.

nodes.name: reconcile-core.ts
nodes.summary: The delete-extras engine for the final under-freeze reconcile: computes org-scoped PK-set diffs (target minus source) for eligible mutable non-audit tables, and executes the deletes children-before-parents in one owner transaction with a large-count fail-closed guard and orphan-probe rollback.
nodes.languageNotes: Closure parents and other orgs' rows appear in neither strict-scoped PK set, so they can never become delete candidates by construction.

nodes.name: upsert.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the UPSERT SQL builders and DataClassification dedupe: append-only DO NOTHING vs mutable guarded DO UPDATE, the force (exact) mode dropping the updated_at guard, composite-PK conflict targets, and dedupe rank/marking retention; includes an optional live-DB connectivity check.

nodes.name: upsert.ts
nodes.summary: Pure idempotent-replay UPSERT SQL builders plus the DataClassification dedupe-with-audit: append-only models get ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, mutable models get last-writer-wins DO UPDATE guarded by updated_at, and a force mode (final reconcile only) overwrites unconditionally to match the frozen source exactly.
nodes.languageNotes: Statement-per-row parameterized SQL keeps numeric values as exact strings and yields precise inserted/updated/skipped counts — correctness over batch speed.

nodes.name: watermark.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for watermark derivation and state handling: updated_at/created_at/full-scan column selection, strictly-greater delta WHERE fragments, observed-max advancement, and state-file validation.

nodes.name: watermark.ts
nodes.summary: Watermark derivation, delta WHERE-clause building, and state advancement for the incremental soak-sync: mutable tables use updated_at, append-only tables use created_at, tables with neither are full-scanned every cycle, and watermarks advance to the max value observed in exported rows so no clock-skew window exists.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses strictly-greater comparison plus observed-max advancement: rows sharing the max timestamp are re-scanned next cycle and UPSERT idempotently — loss-proof by construction.

nodes.name: reconcile-org.mjs
nodes.summary: The final reconcile runner, executed once under source write-freeze: performs a full idempotent force import, deletes org-scoped rows present in target but not source (children-before-parents, fail-closed on large counts), runs the in-transaction orphan probe with rollback on any dangling FK, then invokes the verify gate.

nodes.name: soak-sync.mjs
nodes.summary: Incremental watermark delta replay runner: loads per-table watermark state, delta-exports only rows changed since the last cycle via the shared export core, idempotently imports them via the shared import core, and persists advanced watermarks; optionally loops on an interval to keep v2 caught up during the soak so the freeze window stays tiny.
nodes.languageNotes: Deletes are invisible to a watermark delta by design — removing deleted rows is the final reconcile's job.

nodes.name: verify-org.mjs
nodes.summary: The hard flip gate: read-only comparison of the source org against the migrated v2 org that fails on any mismatch — exact per-model row counts (with DataClassification dedupe adjustment), per-row money equality, the CUI/FOUO marking invariant, sampled sha256 content checksums, and the orphan probe.

nodes.name: computeExtras
nodes.summary: Pure set difference returning the PKs present in the target org-scope but absent from the source — the rows deleted at the source that still linger in the target.

nodes.name: computeDeletePlans
nodes.summary: For each delete-eligible plan, fetches the strict org-scoped PK sets from source and target and computes the per-table lists of extra PKs to delete, re-asserting the by-name delete guards.

nodes.name: executeDeletes
nodes.summary: Executes the delete plans children-before-parents in one owner transaction under session_replication_role=replica, enforces the large-count fail-closed threshold, runs the orphan probe after the deletes, and rolls the whole reconcile back on any dangling FK.

nodes.name: buildUpsert
nodes.summary: Builds one parameterized idempotent UPSERT statement for a row: append-only plans get ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, mutable plans get DO UPDATE guarded by EXCLUDED.updated_at unless force mode drops the guard for the exact under-freeze reconcile; the conflict target uses the full (possibly composite) primary key.

nodes.name: dedupeClassifications
nodes.summary: Collapses duplicate DataClassification rows to one ceiling per org, keeping the highest level (by rank) with its markings, and returns both the surviving rows and an audit record of the dropped duplicates and markings.

nodes.name: watermarkColumnFor
nodes.summary: Selects a plan's watermark column: updated_at for mutable tables, created_at for append-only tables that have it, or none (full scan every cycle) when neither exists.

nodes.name: deltaWhereFragment
nodes.summary: Builds the strictly-greater watermark WHERE fragment and bind value that the export core ANDs onto the strict org-scope SELECT, so a delta can only narrow the result.

nodes.name: advanceWatermark
nodes.summary: Advances a table's watermark to the maximum value actually observed in the exported rows (never a wall clock), eliminating any clock-skew window at the cost of harmlessly re-scanning rows that share the max timestamp.

nodes.name: emptyState
nodes.summary: Returns a fresh empty watermark state object for a first sync.

nodes.name: watermarksForOrg
nodes.summary: Returns (creating if absent) the per-table watermark map for one org within the state object.

nodes.name: assertValidState
nodes.summary: Validates a parsed watermark state file's shape (org map of table-to-ISO-string maps) and throws on anything malformed so a corrupt state cannot silently skip rows.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Drives the four reconcile phases: full force-mode idempotent import of the frozen source, delete-extras via PK-set diff in one owner transaction, the in-transaction orphan probe with rollback on failure, and finally spawns the verify gate whose clean exit is the flip precondition.

nodes.name: runVerify
nodes.summary: Spawns verify-org.mjs as a child process against the source and target and resolves with its exit status, making the verify gate part of the reconcile run.

nodes.name: loadState
nodes.summary: Loads and validates the JSON watermark state file, returning a fresh empty state when the file does not exist (a missing state means a full first sync).

nodes.name: runCycle
nodes.summary: Executes one delta cycle: builds per-table watermark delta filters, delta-exports the changed rows plus referential closure via the shared export core, idempotently imports them via the shared import core, and advances each table's watermark to the observed max.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses CLI args, builds the model plans and watermark columns, then runs a single delta cycle or repeats it on the configured interval in loop mode, persisting the watermark state after each cycle.

nodes.name: normalizeNumericString
nodes.summary: Normalizes a Postgres numeric string (sign, leading zeros, trailing fraction zeros) so exact Decimal values compare equal regardless of formatting.

nodes.name: moneyEqual
nodes.summary: Compares a source money value to its target: exact normalized-string equality for Decimal sources, round-to-4-places comparison for Float sources — never an aggregate SUM.

nodes.name: cuiFouoOrgCount
nodes.summary: Counts the orgs bearing any CUI/FOUO marking in a database, used to assert the marking invariant holds across the migration.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs the full verify suite across source and target: per-model exact org-scoped row counts (with the DataClassification dedupe adjustment), per-row PK-joined money equality, the CUI/FOUO marking invariant, sampled per-row sha256 checksums, and the orphan probe — exiting non-zero on any mismatch.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Org-level PM dashboard server page that authenticates the user, loads org-wide milestones, KPIs, goals, risks, deliverables, blockers, change requests, and CLIN burn data in parallel, then serializes them for the PmDashboard component.
nodes.languageNotes: Next.js App Router async server component using Promise.all to fan out seven Prisma queries before rendering.

nodes.name: OrgPmDashboardPage
nodes.summary: Default-exported async page that resolves the org by slug, guards auth, batch-loads all PM tracker data across the org, and renders PmDashboard with ISO-serialized props.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Project-scoped PM dashboard server page that loads a single project's milestones, KPIs, risks, deliverables, blockers, change requests, CLIN burn, and staffing compliance summary for the PmDashboard component.
nodes.languageNotes: Adds project-level staffing and compliance summarization on top of the org-level dashboard's data loading pattern.

nodes.name: ProjectPmDashboardPage
nodes.summary: Default-exported async page that resolves the project by org slug and key, batch-loads all project PM tracker data plus staffing, computes a compliance summary, and renders PmDashboard.

nodes.name: combined-export.ts
nodes.summary: Merges multiple per-tracker populated XLSX templates into one combined workbook: renames sheets to fit Excel limits, rewrites cross-sheet formulas, deep-copies worksheets with styles, and repairs surrogate-pair corruption in the emitted XML.
nodes.languageNotes: Post-processes the ExcelJS output at the ZIP/XML level with JSZip to fix formula text corrupted by unpaired UTF-16 surrogates — a workaround for an ExcelJS encoding bug.

nodes.name: makeSheetName
nodes.summary: Generates a unique, Excel-legal worksheet name (31-char limit, forbidden characters stripped) by prefixing the tracker code and truncating or suffixing on collision.

nodes.name: rewriteFormula
nodes.summary: Rewrites sheet references inside an Excel formula string to match renamed sheets, handling both quoted and bare sheet-name reference forms.

nodes.name: copyWorksheet
nodes.summary: Deep-copies a worksheet into the destination workbook cell by cell, preserving column widths, styles, and merged cells while rewriting formulas via the rename map and logging them for later repair.

nodes.name: repairSurrogateCorruption
nodes.summary: Opens the generated XLSX as a ZIP, scans worksheet XML for Unicode replacement characters left by broken surrogate pairs, and restores the original formula text from the pre-corruption formula log.

nodes.name: buildCombinedWorkbook
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the combined export: builds each tracker's populated template, plans unique sheet names, copies every worksheet into a single output workbook, and returns the corruption-repaired buffer.

nodes.name: kpi-derive.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for applyKpiAutoValue, verifying that KPI auto-source metrics (velocity, cycle time, throughput) map to the correct derived values.

nodes.name: kpi-derive.ts
nodes.summary: Derives auto-computed KPI values from board execution data: computes velocity, completion rate, cycle time, and throughput from work items and intervals, then applies them to KPIs configured with an auto source.

nodes.name: computeExecutionMetrics
nodes.summary: Queries work items and interval counts to compute execution metrics — completion percentage, average velocity per interval, mean cycle time in days, and a windowed throughput function.

nodes.name: applyKpiAutoValue
nodes.summary: Pure mapper that resolves a KPI's auto-source identifier (velocity, cycle-time, throughput, completion) to the matching value from precomputed execution metrics.

nodes.name: loadKpisWithDerived
nodes.summary: Loads KPIs for a scope and, when any use an auto source, computes execution metrics once and overlays derived current values onto those KPIs.

nodes.name: schedule.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for deriveMilestone, using fixture builders to verify derived progress, health, and status across linked work-item column states and due dates.

nodes.name: ms
nodes.summary: Test fixture builder that constructs a milestone object with sensible defaults and optional overrides for due date, actual date, status, and linked work items.

nodes.name: staffing.ts
nodes.summary: Staffing roster and compliance logic: joins project members with employee records to evaluate CAC, training, access, and NDA compliance per person, with an aggregate compliance summary for dashboards.

nodes.name: summarizeCompliance
nodes.summary: Aggregates staffing rows into compliance counts and an overall percentage across CAC, training, access, and NDA checks.

nodes.name: loadStaffing
nodes.summary: Loads project members, matches them to employee HR records, and produces sorted staffing rows with per-person compliance flags, classification, and optionally burdened cost rates.

nodes.name: layout.tsx
nodes.summary: Per-organization dashboard layout that streams children immediately while a Suspense-deferred server component looks up the org's primary theme color (cached Prisma query) and injects org-specific CSS variables via an inline style tag; also mounts the client-side What's New changelog modal.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Next.js 16 patterns: awaited params inside a Suspense boundary for instant-shell rendering, and the 'use cache' directive on the theme lookup.

nodes.name: OrgScopedLayout
nodes.summary: Default-exported layout component that renders children immediately, wraps the theme style injection in a Suspense boundary with a null fallback to avoid unstyled flashes, and appends the WhatsNew client island.

nodes.name: OrgThemeStyle
nodes.summary: Async server component that awaits the orgSlug param, fetches the organization's themePrimary color, and renders a raw style tag with the generated org theme CSS, or nothing when no override exists.

nodes.name: contrast.ts
nodes.summary: WCAG color-contrast math utilities: converts hex to RGB, computes relative luminance and contrast ratio between two colors, and checks AA compliance for normal or large text.

nodes.name: contrastRatio
nodes.summary: Computes the WCAG contrast ratio between two hex colors from their relative luminances.

nodes.name: passesAA
nodes.summary: Returns whether a foreground/background hex pair meets the WCAG AA contrast threshold (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text).

nodes.name: contrast.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the WCAG contrast utilities, verifying contrast ratio calculations and AA pass/fail thresholds against known color pairs.

nodes.name: derive.ts
nodes.summary: Derives a full org theme palette from a single primary brand hex color: hex/RGB/HSL conversions, contrast-safe foreground selection, lightness adjustment to guarantee readability on light and dark surfaces, plus tint and hover variant generation.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure functional color math with no dependencies beyond the sibling contrast module; ensureOnSurface iteratively nudges HSL lightness until the contrast ratio target is met.

nodes.name: rgbToHex
nodes.summary: Converts an RGB triple to an uppercase hex color string, clamping each channel to the 0-255 range.

nodes.name: hexToHsl
nodes.summary: Converts a hex color to an HSL triple for lightness-based theme adjustments.

nodes.name: hslToHex
nodes.summary: Converts an HSL triple back to a hex color string using the standard hue-to-RGB algorithm.

nodes.name: readableForeground
nodes.summary: Validates a hex color and returns the higher-contrast foreground (light or dark) to render on top of it, or null for invalid input.

nodes.name: ensureOnSurface
nodes.summary: Adjusts a color's HSL lightness step-by-step (darkening or lightening) until it reaches sufficient contrast against a given surface color, returning the first passing shade.

nodes.name: themedPrimary
nodes.summary: Builds the complete theme derivation for a primary brand color: contrast-corrected light and dark surface variants plus matching foreground colors for each, or null for invalid hex input.

nodes.name: deriveTint
nodes.summary: Produces a translucent tint (rgb components) of the primary color for subtle backgrounds.

nodes.name: deriveHover
nodes.summary: Derives a slightly darker hover-state variant of the primary color by reducing HSL lightness.

nodes.name: derive.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the theme derivation module, asserting that derived primary variants and foregrounds meet contrast requirements and that tint/hover derivations behave as expected.

nodes.name: server-styles.ts
nodes.summary: Server-side generator of org theme CSS: turns an organization's primary color into :root CSS custom property rules for light mode, dark mode, and prefers-color-scheme media query fallback.

nodes.name: orgThemeCss
nodes.summary: Given an optional org primary color, derives the themed palette and emits CSS rules setting --primary, hover, and tint variables for light and dark roots, or null when no valid color is provided.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Next.js API route handling POST uploads of bank statement files (CSV or OFX) for a specific org bank account, enforcing RBAC permission checks before parsing and importing the transactions.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Authenticates the caller, verifies the bank account belongs to the org, reads the uploaded statement file from multipart form data, dispatches to the CSV or OFX parser based on format, and imports the parsed transactions.

nodes.name: import.ts
nodes.summary: Core bank transaction import logic: fingerprints each parsed transaction with a SHA-256 hash for idempotent dedupe, applies org-defined categorization rules, and bulk-inserts the results via Prisma.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses SHA-256 fingerprints (account|date|amount|description) with Prisma createMany + skipDuplicates semantics to make statement re-imports idempotent.

nodes.name: fingerprintTxn
nodes.summary: Computes a SHA-256 fingerprint from bank account id, posted date, amount, and description to uniquely identify a transaction for duplicate detection.

nodes.name: importTransactions
nodes.summary: Loads the org's bank rules, maps parsed transactions to database rows with fingerprints and rule-derived categorization, and bulk-inserts them into the bank transaction table.

nodes.name: csv.ts
nodes.summary: CSV bank statement parser with a hand-rolled quote-aware CSV splitter and a column-mapping layer that normalizes rows (single amount or separate credit/debit columns) into ParsedTxn records.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements its own quoted-field CSV tokenizer rather than pulling in a CSV library, and supports both signed-amount and credit/debit dual-column mappings via Decimal arithmetic.

nodes.name: splitCsv
nodes.summary: Tokenizes raw CSV text into rows of cells, handling quoted fields, escaped quotes, and blank-line skipping.

nodes.name: parseCsv
nodes.summary: Converts CSV rows into normalized ParsedTxn objects using a caller-supplied column mapping, computing signed amounts from either an amount column or credit-minus-debit columns.

nodes.name: ofx.ts
nodes.summary: OFX bank statement parser that extracts the bank transfer list from an OFX document and normalizes each transaction (id, posted date, amount, description) into ParsedTxn records, including OFX-specific date decoding.
nodes.languageNotes: Handles both ISO-like and compact YYYYMMDD OFX date formats, converting them to UTC dates.

nodes.name: parseOfx
nodes.summary: Parses OFX file content, reads the bank transaction list, and maps each entry to a normalized ParsedTxn with external id, UTC posted date, decimal amount, and trimmed description.

nodes.name: rules.ts
nodes.summary: Bank categorization rule engine: matches transactions against org-defined rules on direction (money in/out), description substring, and amount magnitude bounds, returning the first matching rule's categorization.

nodes.name: matchRule
nodes.summary: Tests whether a single rule matches a transaction by checking money-in/money-out direction, case-insensitive description containment, and min/max amount magnitude bounds.

nodes.name: applyRules
nodes.summary: Iterates an ordered rule list and returns the first rule that matches the transaction, or null when none apply.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the ParsedTxn type — the normalized bank transaction shape (external id, posted date, signed Prisma.Decimal amount, description) shared by all statement parsers and the import pipeline.

nodes.name: filter.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the serialisable JQL-lite typed filter model for cross-project work-item queries: the WorkItemFilter interface, parent/date-range/custom-field sub-filters, sort whitelist, and sentinel constants like UNASSIGNED and NO_INTERVAL plus page-size caps.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure TypeScript types plus a few const sentinels; designed to round-trip through URLs, saved views, and board config as plain JSON. Semantics mirror JQL: AND across fields, OR within a multi-select field.

nodes.name: build-where.ts
nodes.summary: Pure, synchronous translator from a WorkItemFilter into a Prisma WHERE clause and ORDER BY, intersecting requested project ids with the caller's RBAC-allowed projects and handling sentinels (unassigned, no-interval), date ranges, free text, and custom-field JSON constraints.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately DB-free and side-effect-free so the filter-to-WHERE translation can be exhaustively unit-tested; RBAC scoping is folded in via an allowedProjectIds argument rather than resolved here.

nodes.name: parse.ts
nodes.summary: Parses URL search params into a validated WorkItemFilter plus sort and pagination, exposing zod schemas (workItemFilterSchema, workItemQuerySchema) and parseSearchParams with comma-separated multi-value handling, custom-field param decoding, and clamped page sizes.

nodes.name: build-where.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for buildWorkItemWhere covering RBAC project-scope intersection, sentinel handling for unassigned and no-interval, parent-mode filters, date ranges, free-text search, and custom-field constraints.

nodes.name: parse.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for parseSearchParams verifying URL-param decoding into a WorkItemFilter, including comma-separated multi-values, priority whitelisting, sort-field fallback, custom-field param parsing, and page-size clamping.

nodes.name: buildWorkItemWhere
nodes.summary: Converts a WorkItemFilter plus the caller's allowed project ids into a Prisma WorkItemWhereInput, ANDing distinct fields, ORing within multi-selects, and expanding sentinels, parent modes, date ranges, text search, watcher, and custom-field JSON constraints.

nodes.name: buildDateRange
nodes.summary: Builds an inclusive gte/lte Prisma date constraint from a DateRange, tolerating open-ended bounds and dropping unparseable edges.

nodes.name: parseDate
nodes.summary: Parses an ISO date or datetime string into a Date, treating bare YYYY-MM-DD values as day boundaries depending on whether it is a lower or upper bound, and returning undefined for invalid input.

nodes.name: buildOrderBy
nodes.summary: Maps a whitelisted WorkItemSort into a stable Prisma orderBy array, falling back to a deterministic default ordering when the sort field is absent or unsupported.

nodes.name: parseSearchParams
nodes.summary: Decodes URLSearchParams into a WorkItemFilter with sort and clamped pagination, whitelisting priorities and sort fields, reading multi-value and date-range params, and delegating custom-field params to a dedicated parser.

nodes.name: parseCustomFieldParams
nodes.summary: Parses repeated cf query params of the form key:KIND:value into CustomFieldFilter entries, validating the kind against the supported set and coercing CHECKBOX values to booleans.

nodes.name: parity-lib.ts
nodes.summary: Pure, side-effect-free helpers for the cutover schema-parity and provenance hard gate: a stable sha256 fingerprint over prod's _prisma_migrations history, a tolerant JSON/CSV migration-row parser, the pg_constraint probe SQL asserting the classification FK, and the provenance baseline record builder.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately I/O-free (timestamp passed in, no fs/db access) so every gate predicate is unit-testable; hash uses length-prefix framing to prevent concatenation collisions.

nodes.name: parity-lib.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the cutover parity helpers, verifying hash determinism (order-independence), tamper sensitivity (checksum edits, added/removed migrations), JSON/CSV row parsing, FK probe SQL construction, and baseline record assembly.

nodes.name: parity-gate.mjs
nodes.summary: Fail-closed CLI hard gate for the v2 cutover: restores a prod pg_dump into a scratch Postgres, runs prisma migrate diff against a shadow DB built by replaying prisma/migrations (must be empty), independently asserts the data_classifications.project_id foreign key, and writes an auditable provenance baseline to compliance/provenance/prod-baseline.json.
nodes.languageNotes: An .mjs script run under tsx so it can import .ts helpers directly; diffs against a migrations-replay shadow DB rather than schema.prisma because raw-SQL-only objects (generated columns, HNSW indexes, triggers) are absent from the datamodel.

nodes.name: computeMigrationHistoryHash
nodes.summary: Computes a stable sha256 over prod's ordered (migration_name, checksum) pairs, sorting by name and length-prefix-framing each field so the provenance fingerprint is order-independent and collision-resistant.

nodes.name: parseMigrationRows
nodes.summary: Tolerant parser that accepts a prod _prisma_migrations export as either a JSON array or psql --csv output and normalizes it to MigrationRow objects.

nodes.name: splitCsvLine
nodes.summary: Minimal quoted-field-aware CSV line splitter used by parseMigrationRows to handle psql --csv output.

nodes.name: classificationFkProbeSql
nodes.summary: Builds the read-only pg_constraint EXISTS query asserting that the single-column foreign key data_classifications.project_id -> projects.id is present in the restored prod snapshot.

nodes.name: buildBaselineRecord
nodes.summary: Assembles the provenance baseline JSON object (migration-history hash, prod commit, gate verdict, timestamp) without performing any I/O; the caller writes it to disk.

nodes.name: parseArgs
nodes.summary: Parses the gate's CLI flags (dump path, scratch/shadow URLs, stamp, optional migrations export, commit, output path, --no-write) into an args map, failing on unknown flags.

nodes.name: psql
nodes.summary: Runs a SQL statement against the scratch database via spawnSync psql, failing closed on non-zero exit or missing binary.

nodes.name: restoreDump
nodes.summary: Restores the schema-only prod pg_dump into the throwaway scratch database via psql, failing closed on any restore error.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the two-part hard gate: validates args and inputs, restores the prod dump into scratch, runs the prisma migrate diff parity check, probes the classification FK, then hashes the migration history and writes the provenance baseline file, exiting non-zero on any failure.

nodes.name: runMigrateDiff
nodes.summary: Replays prisma/migrations into the throwaway shadow database and runs prisma migrate diff between the restored prod snapshot and that reference schema, returning the diff SQL (empty means parity).

nodes.name: probeClassificationFk
nodes.summary: Connects to the scratch database with node-postgres and executes the classification FK probe SQL, returning whether the data_classifications.project_id foreign key exists.

nodes.name: levels.ts
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for data-classification level metadata (PUBLIC through CONFIDENTIAL): labels, U.S. banner-color standard, badge/banner Tailwind palettes, sensitivity ranking, and marking helpers. Deliberately free of Prisma imports so both client and server components can consume it.
nodes.languageNotes: String-union type mirrors the Prisma ClassificationLevel enum instead of importing @prisma/client, keeping the module safe for client-side bundles. Legacy FOUO level is retained for old data but renders as CUI and is excluded from the selectable list.

nodes.name: classificationLabel
nodes.summary: Resolves the display label for a classification level, mapping the retired FOUO marking to its CUI replacement and falling back to the raw level string.

nodes.name: isMarkingLevel
nodes.summary: Returns whether a classification level warrants a visible marking banner, using the rank table to include FOUO/CUI and above while exempting PUBLIC and UNCLASSIFIED.

nodes.name: classification-banner.tsx
nodes.summary: Server component that renders the high-contrast classification marking strip for a project or org, looking up the effective data classification in Prisma and only displaying a banner when the level meets the marking threshold.
nodes.languageNotes: Async React Server Component that queries Prisma directly (dataClassification findUnique/findFirst via Promise.all) rather than fetching through an API route.

nodes.name: ClassificationBanner
nodes.summary: Async component that resolves the effective classification for the given org/project from the database, skips rendering for non-marking levels, and outputs a color-coded banner strip with the uppercased label and any control markings joined in banner format.

nodes.name: levels.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the classification level metadata module, covering label resolution (including the FOUO-to-CUI aliasing), selectable-level filtering, color-standard consistency, rank ordering, and the marking-level threshold.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Docker build-context exclusion list that keeps node_modules, build output, docs, deploy rollback dumps, plugin checkouts, and all secret material (.env files, keys, certs) out of the image build, both for cache hygiene and to prevent secrets from riding into the build stage via COPY.

nodes.name: docker-compose.acceptance.yml
nodes.summary: Minimal compose stack (project cosmos-accept) that boots a single throwaway pgvector Postgres on host port 55432 for the native-connectors Docker acceptance run, deliberately omitting MinIO, pgBackRest archiving, and Caddy.

nodes.name: accept-postgres
nodes.summary: Acceptance-test Postgres container reusing the cosmos-v2-postgres:dev pgvector image with plain postgres command (no WAL archiving), published on 55432 with a pg_isready healthcheck.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Primary cosmos-v2 orchestration stack: base services (pgvector+pgBackRest Postgres, MinIO object storage with TLS bootstrap, Prisma migrate one-shot, the Next.js app, Caddy reverse proxy) plus profile-gated groups — ops one-shots for backup, audit WORM export, hash-chain verification, retention purge, and vault-key rotation; an observability stack (OTel collector, Prometheus, Jaeger, Grafana); a self-hosted Nango OAuth broker; and a cutover proxy for per-tenant v1-to-v2 migration.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavily compliance-annotated (NIST 800-171 / AU-9, CP-9/10, SI-4 control references) with digest-pinned images, least-privilege DB roles per service, named volumes for pgBackRest stanza state, and $$-escaped shell interpolation so container-time env overrides survive compose config-time expansion.

nodes.name: cosmos-postgres
nodes.summary: Primary pgvector Postgres with pgBackRest layered on for WAL archiving to the in-boundary MinIO S3 repo; runs with archive_mode on, a shared Unix-socket volume for local-mode backups, first-boot init scripts, and a named pgBackRest state volume so the stanza marker survives container recreation.

nodes.name: minio-certs
nodes.summary: One-shot Alpine+openssl job that generates a self-signed TLS certificate into the shared certs volume so MinIO serves HTTPS; the cert lives only in the volume, never in git.

nodes.name: cosmos-minio
nodes.summary: In-boundary S3-compatible MinIO object storage serving HTTPS with the self-signed internal cert; the S3 API stays on the internal compose network while only the operator console is published on 9001.

nodes.name: minio-init
nodes.summary: One-shot mc job that creates the three buckets (including the object-locked COMPLIANCE-retention audit-worm bucket) and two least-privilege service accounts; postgres and the app gate on its successful completion.

nodes.name: cosmos-migrate
nodes.summary: One-shot Prisma migration runner using the dedicated cosmos-v2-migrate:dev image (Dockerfile migrate target), executing schema migrations as the owner role once Postgres is healthy.

nodes.name: cosmos
nodes.summary: The cosmos-v2 Next.js application container: connects to Postgres as the least-privilege cosmos_app role, uses MinIO S3 for uploads with an internal CA trust chain, exports observe-only OTel telemetry, and optionally talks to the internal Nango broker; gated on migrations completing and MinIO being healthy.

nodes.name: reverse-proxy
nodes.summary: Caddy public front door on 80/443 with automatic HTTPS (Let's Encrypt or an internal ACME CA for airgap), persisting ACME account and issued certs in named volumes to avoid rate-limit re-issuance on redeploys.

nodes.name: cutover-proxy
nodes.summary: Profile-gated second Caddy instance (host 8091) that fronts the v1 and v2 stacks during per-tenant cutover; driven live through its internal-only admin API by the cutover proxy-control scripts for freeze/flip/rollback.

nodes.name: cosmos-backup
nodes.summary: Ops-profile one-shot pgBackRest backup job (full weekly / incremental daily) that shares the Postgres image, pgdata volume, Unix socket, and stanza state so it can run local-mode backups to the MinIO S3 repo without a pgBackRest TLS/SSH server.

nodes.name: audit-worm-export
nodes.summary: Ops-profile one-shot that dumps audit_logs and egress_decisions since the last export to the object-locked cosmos-audit-worm bucket with a signed sha256 manifest, reading as the SELECT-only cosmos_app role and writing with a write-only WORM key.

nodes.name: rotate-vault-key
nodes.summary: Ops-profile one-shot that re-wraps every vault-sealed secret (IdP client secrets) to the keyring's active kid via tsx against the same vault TypeScript the app uses, enabling rotate-then-retire key cycles as the least-privilege role.

nodes.name: verify-audit-chain
nodes.summary: Ops-profile one-shot tamper-evidence gate that calls the in-DB verify_audit_chain() over audit_logs and egress_decisions, also validating the latest retention-purge checkpoint HMAC, and exits non-zero if either hash-chain is broken.

nodes.name: purge-audit
nodes.summary: Ops-profile one-shot and the only sanctioned audit-delete path: records a signed chain checkpoint then purges audit rows older than the retention floor in one owner transaction, refusing unless the purged range is already WORM-anchored offsite and never dropping below the 1095-day gov floor.

nodes.name: otel-collector
nodes.summary: Observability-profile OTel Collector (contrib, distroless) receiving OTLP from the app and exporting metrics to a Prometheus scrape endpoint and traces to Jaeger; internal network only, no host ports.

nodes.name: prometheus
nodes.summary: Observability-profile Prometheus scraping the OTel collector and sidecars, holding the alert rules, with persistent TSDB storage and the UI published on 9090.

nodes.name: jaeger
nodes.summary: Observability-profile Jaeger all-in-one trace store and UI (16686) with OTLP ingest enabled for the collector; ingest ports stay internal to the compose network.

nodes.name: grafana
nodes.summary: Observability-profile Grafana (host 3009) with provisioned Prometheus and Jaeger datasources plus the COSMOS dashboard, locked down with no sign-up, no anonymous access, and analytics/phone-home disabled.

nodes.name: cosmos-nango-db
nodes.summary: Nango-profile dedicated Postgres 16 (separate from cosmos-postgres, since Nango owns its own schema and migrations), internal-only with data on a named volume.

nodes.name: cosmos-nango-redis
nodes.summary: Nango-profile Redis 7.2.4 cache for the Nango server, internal-only with no host port.

nodes.name: cosmos-nango-server
nodes.summary: Nango-profile self-hosted OAuth/API-key broker (hosted-0.70.6, commercial-only connector breadth) reached by the app over the internal network; the API server and Connect UI are host-published on 3013/3019 for the OAuth grant flow, with dashboard basic-auth and Elasticsearch logging disabled.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Builds the Cosmos Postgres image from a digest-pinned pgvector base, adding pgBackRest for WAL archiving and base backups to the in-boundary MinIO S3 repo, and wrapping the stock entrypoint so the pgBackRest config is rendered from environment variables at container start (no secrets baked into the image).
nodes.languageNotes: Single-stage build pinned by image digest for supply-chain hygiene; runtime config is generated at startup by an entrypoint wrapper instead of being baked into the image, keeping secrets out of layers.

nodes.name: teams-digest.yml
nodes.summary: Weekday-scheduled workflow that POSTs to the org's Teams digest endpoint to publish a one-message 24-hour summary; the endpoint short-circuits unless the Teams integration and dailyDigest toggle are active, and the job no-ops until COSMOS_* config exists.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Template of the 40+ runtime environment variables the platform needs: Postgres/Prisma URLs, Anthropic API key and model, VAPID web-push keys, Google OAuth, Resend email, S3/MinIO storage (including WORM audit buckets), pgBackRest, Grafana, and the Nango integration stack. Documents which secrets must be provided at runtime without shipping real values.
nodes.languageNotes: Groups variables by subsystem (auth, storage, backup, observability, integrations), effectively serving as a map of every external service the app touches.

nodes.name: .gitleaks.toml
nodes.summary: Gitleaks secret-scanning configuration that extends the full default ruleset and adds a single narrow allowlist for the TEMP_PASSWORD_ALPHABET literal in src/lib/auth/temp-password.ts, a known false positive of the generic-api-key rule.

nodes.name: components.json
nodes.summary: shadcn CLI configuration using the base-nova style with RSC and TSX enabled, Tailwind CSS via src/app/globals.css, lucide icons, and path aliases (@/components, @/lib, @/hooks) matching the tsconfig @/* mapping.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript compiler configuration with strict mode, bundler module resolution, noEmit type-checking, the Next.js language-service plugin, and a single @/* path alias onto src/ used throughout the codebase.

nodes.name: Chart.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm chart manifest for the cosmos chart — the UDS-native core stack bundling the app, CrunchyData PGO Postgres, MinIO, the migrate hook, and the UDS Package CR, pinned to app release 2.102.2.
nodes.languageNotes: Declares no chart dependencies: the PGO and MinIO operators are installed cluster-wide out-of-chart, and the chart ships only their instances.

nodes.name: values.yaml
nodes.summary: Default (medium) Helm values for the cosmos chart: digest-pinned cosign-verified images, app replica sizing, security posture, Istio exposure via the UDS Package, Keycloak SSO client wiring, MinIO object storage with WORM buckets, PGO PostgresCluster with optional pgBackRest S3 backups, and scheduled audit-chain verification ops.
nodes.languageNotes: Images are referenced by immutable sha256 digest (multi-arch index) rather than tags, inheriting the supply-chain guarantee from the cosign signing pipeline; sizing and hardening are layered on via separate override files.

nodes.name: values-large.yaml
nodes.summary: Large-profile Helm values overlay for HA/production scale: raises the app to 3 replicas with 500m CPU / 1-2Gi memory, with placeholders for future Postgres HA and distributed MinIO knobs.

nodes.name: values-small.yaml
nodes.summary: Small-profile Helm values overlay for single-node/dev footprints: a single app replica with 100m CPU / 384-768Mi memory, with placeholders for minimal Postgres and MinIO sizing.

nodes.name: values-posture-dod.yaml
nodes.summary: DoD-compliant hardened posture overlay that flips posture to dod, enabling Iron Bank (registry1) images, Postgres FIPS mode with 1095-day audit retention, default-deny network policies, enforced Keycloak SSO, and external GovCloud S3 storage; orthogonal to and combinable with the sizing overlays.
nodes.languageNotes: Posture (hardening) and sizing are deliberately orthogonal overlay dimensions — this file composes with values-large.yaml or values-small.yaml via multiple -f flags.

nodes.name: app.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template defining the cosmos web Deployment (Next.js standalone, non-root, UDS-compliant) and its ClusterIP Service on port 3000, wiring env for the least-privilege cosmos_app Postgres role over verified TLS, MinIO S3 storage, and SOPS-managed SSO/WORM secrets.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Kubernetes $(VAR) env substitution to inject the app password from a Secret directly into DATABASE_URL, and distinct component:web labels to avoid colliding with MinIO's Service selector.

nodes.name: migrate-job.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm pre-install/pre-upgrade hook Job that first creates the least-privilege cosmos_app LOGIN role via a psql initContainer, then runs `prisma migrate deploy` as the cosmos superuser from the dedicated migrate image to apply all database migrations.
nodes.languageNotes: Helm hook annotations (pre-install,pre-upgrade, weight 10, before-hook-creation delete policy) sequence schema migration ahead of app rollout; the initContainer polls Postgres readiness before role creation.

nodes.name: minio-init.yaml
nodes.summary: Post-install/post-upgrade hook Job that uses the MinIO mc client to idempotently create the uploads, pgBackRest backup, and object-locked audit-WORM buckets (with COMPLIANCE retention), and provisions the least-privilege app service account.
nodes.languageNotes: The audit bucket is created with --with-lock and a default COMPLIANCE retention period, giving WORM (write-once-read-many) guarantees for audit evidence.

nodes.name: minio.yaml
nodes.summary: Helm template deploying a single-replica MinIO StatefulSet with a persistent volume claim template and a Service exposing the S3 API (9000) and web console (9001), hardened to pass the UDS Pepr pod-security baseline without exemptions.

nodes.name: ops-jobs.yaml
nodes.summary: CronJob for government audit/compliance operations that periodically runs the verify-audit-chain script from the migrate image as the least-privilege cosmos_app role over verified Postgres TLS, validating the tamper-evident audit log chain.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses component:ops labels (without an instance label) specifically to keep these pods out of MinIO's Service selector; network connectivity relies on the UDS Package's IntraNamespace and KubeAPI egress allows.

nodes.name: postgrescluster.yaml
nodes.summary: CrunchyData PGO PostgresCluster resource provisioning Postgres with pgvector, the cosmos superuser role, and pgBackRest backups to a local volume repo plus an optional TLS-verified MinIO S3 repo configured from a SOPS-managed secret.
nodes.languageNotes: The cosmos_app role is deliberately not declared here because PGO user names cannot contain underscores; it is created by the migrate hook instead. repo2 requires uri-style=path for MinIO S3 compatibility.

nodes.name: uds-package.yaml
nodes.summary: UDS Package resource that the uds-operator converts into an Istio VirtualService on the tenant gateway plus default-deny NetworkPolicies, with explicit allow rules for intra-namespace Postgres/MinIO traffic, Patroni's KubeAPI access, Keycloak OIDC egress, and pgBackRest S3 egress, and optionally declares the Keycloak SSO client.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavily annotated with operational gotchas: the KubeAPI egress prevents Patroni crash-loops under default-deny, and the pgBackRest allow is intentionally portless because the Tenant Service's 443-to-9000 DNAT would silently drop port-scoped traffic.

nodes.name: alerts.yml
nodes.summary: Prometheus alerting rules implementing the SI-4 (NIST 800-171 3.14.6-3.14.7) must-have signals: critical alerts when the CUI-blind egress chokepoint errors or the in-boundary CUI classifier goes down, plus a warning when any observability scrape target reports up == 0.
nodes.languageNotes: Alerts use increase() over 5m windows with for: 0m so any error immediately fires; both critical rules document that failures fail closed (safe) but degrade the egress tripwire.

nodes.name: otel-collector.yaml
nodes.summary: OpenTelemetry Collector (contrib) configuration that receives OTLP traces and metrics from the cosmos app and fans them out: metrics to a Prometheus exporter on :8889 and traces to Jaeger via OTLP/gRPC, with memory-limiter and batch processors plus a health-check extension. Observe-only by design — telemetry is already CUI-stripped by the app.
nodes.languageNotes: Exposes the collector's own internal metrics on :8888 (pull Prometheus reader) specifically to avoid a false-positive SidecarDown alert; resource_to_telemetry_conversion surfaces resource attributes as metric labels.

nodes.name: prometheus.yml
nodes.summary: Prometheus scrape and alerting configuration for the in-boundary monitoring stack (SI-4): 15s scrape/evaluation intervals, loads alerts.yml as rule_files, and scrapes the OTel Collector (app metrics on :8889 and collector self-telemetry on :8888), Prometheus itself, Jaeger, and Grafana. MinIO scraping is deliberately deferred pending auth provisioning.

nodes.name: cosmos-backup.sh
nodes.summary: Periodic Postgres backup one-shot that renders the pgBackRest config from env, then runs an incremental (or full, via PGBACKREST_BACKUP_TYPE) backup of the 'cosmos' stanza to the MinIO S3 repo, connecting to the live Postgres over a shared socket dir and reading cluster files from the shared pgdata volume.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `exec gosu postgres pgbackrest ...` to replace the shell and drop to the postgres user in one step, keeping the one-shot container's PID 1 clean.

nodes.name: cosmos-stanza-create.sh
nodes.summary: Idempotent first-run helper that creates the pgBackRest 'cosmos' stanza in the MinIO repo, drops the /var/lib/pgbackrest/.stanza-ready marker that enables real WAL archiving in pgbackrest-archive-push.sh, and takes the initial FULL backup.

nodes.name: docker-entrypoint-wrapper.sh
nodes.summary: Entrypoint wrapper for the cosmos Postgres image: renders the pgBackRest config from env when repo credentials are present (warning loudly otherwise), fixes ownership/permissions on the shared socket dir while still root, then execs the stock postgres docker-entrypoint.sh unchanged.
nodes.languageNotes: Performs root-only setup (chown of the shared socket volume) before the stock entrypoint drops privileges to the postgres user — a common pattern for augmenting official images without forking them.

nodes.name: pgbackrest-archive-push.sh
nodes.summary: archive_command wrapper invoked by Postgres for every completed WAL segment; it gates on a local .stanza-ready marker so first-boot bootstrap is never blocked before the stanza exists, and adds a defense-in-depth check on the async spool dir so post-stanza WAL is never silently dropped if the marker goes missing.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately avoids any S3 call on the hot path: the pre-stanza gate is a purely local marker-file check, because a blocking archive_command during the official image's temporary bootstrap server would stall initdb shutdown indefinitely.

nodes.name: render-pgbackrest-conf.sh
nodes.summary: Idempotently renders /etc/pgbackrest/pgbackrest.conf from a template by substituting S3 credentials and the repo cipher passphrase from required env vars, so no secrets are baked into the image; run by both the entrypoint wrapper and the backup one-shot.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses pipe-delimited sed expressions plus an esc() helper that escapes '|' so secrets containing '/' or '&' cannot break the substitution.

nodes.name: .sops.yaml
nodes.summary: SOPS creation-rules config that pins the age public recipient key for every *.enc.yaml file in the deploy/secrets directory, ensuring all committed secrets are encrypted to the same lab-held age identity.
nodes.languageNotes: SOPS matches files via path_regex and encrypts to the listed age recipient; the matching private key lives only on the lab machine and is never committed.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Operational guide for the SOPS+age encrypted Kubernetes secrets: decrypt/apply/edit commands, and a pre-commit invariants table (SSO_VAULT_KEY must decode to exactly 32 bytes for AES-256, rotation must re-key sealed data rather than swap keys blindly).
nodes.languageNotes: Explains why a 48-byte SSO_VAULT_KEY passes casual inspection but crashes SSO at runtime via the KEY_BYTES=32 check in src/lib/crypto/vault.ts, and warns that a wrong key orphans previously sealed data.

nodes.name: cosmos-app-secrets.enc.yaml
nodes.summary: SOPS/age-encrypted Kubernetes Secret carrying the application's runtime credentials in stringData: SSO_VAULT_KEY (AES-256 vault key), WORM_MANIFEST_HMAC_KEY, INTERNAL_ADMINS, and COSMOS_APP_PASSWORD (least-privilege DB role password).
nodes.languageNotes: Every value including apiVersion/kind is stored as ENC[AES256_GCM,...]; the sops block records the age recipient, MAC, and last-modified metadata so the file is safe to commit.

nodes.name: cosmos-pgbackrest-s3.enc.yaml
nodes.summary: SOPS/age-encrypted Kubernetes Secret providing pgBackRest's S3 backup credentials for the PostgreSQL cluster: a ca.crt trust certificate and an s3.conf configuration blob stored as base64 data keys.

nodes.name: AI-CHAT-TEST-PLAN.md
nodes.summary: End-to-end manual validation plan for AI chat phases 1-5: token streaming, persistent CLI pool, Google and Cosmos-internal CRUD tools, rich UI (markdown, abort, model picker, attachments), MCP server settings, and RAG semantic search. Includes cross-cutting checks (audit logs, rate limits, permission gating, security), a test-artifact cleanup list, and a scorecard template.
nodes.languageNotes: Notes that pgvector is not installed, so RAG falls back to JSON token-overlap pseudo-embeddings marked with TODO(rag) in src/lib/rag/embed.ts.

nodes.name: SETTINGS-VALIDATION-PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Comprehensive manual validation checklist for every Cosmos settings surface — user menu, profile, preferences (theme, density, background, layout), themes, custom fields, templates, security (SSO, IP allowlist, SCIM, sessions), compliance, classifications, integrations, webhooks, and audit logs. Ends with cross-cutting checks, negative-path testing, cleanup steps, and a final scorecard template.

nodes.name: 0002-cosmo-agent-per-user-connector-oauth.md
nodes.summary: Proposed (unimplemented) design record for ticket COSMOS-18: migrating COSMO Agent connectors (GitHub, Jira, Slack, Microsoft 365) from shared org-wide credentials to per-user OAuth grants, using the existing Google connector as the reference implementation. Documents the current gap, why auto-implementation was declined (unverifiable external OAuth infra, human-review-gated auth surface), and a three-phase rollout plan with no org-credential fallback.
nodes.languageNotes: A design-only ADR written by the autonomous delivery daemon in lieu of shipping code — records ground truth with exact file/line references so a human implementer starts from verified state.

nodes.name: 2026-07-21-foreman-console-reorg-design.md
nodes.summary: Approved design for reorganizing the Foreman console from a flat stack of ~13 panels into four deep-linkable tabs (Activity, Connections, Build behavior, Automation) and collapsing the duplicate Skills create/import forms into one Compose|Paste 'Add skill' flow. Also folds in a regression fix requiring the console test to mock /foreman/loop-metrics.

nodes.name: 2026-07-21-foreman-console-reorg-plan.md
nodes.summary: Step-by-step TDD implementation plan for the Foreman console tab reorganization: three checkbox tasks covering a new console-tabs.tsx primitive (useTabParam hook + TabList component), wrapping foreman-console.tsx panels into four tab groups with URL-driven state, and merging the skills panel forms into a single Add-skill flow reusing parseSkillMarkdown. Includes exact test code and global constraints (panels moved not modified, no new dependencies).

nodes.name: background-scheduler-substrate.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal for a shared background-job/scheduler substrate: a Postgres-backed durable job queue (pg-boss recommended, hand-rolled Job table as fallback) with an in-process singleton worker, chosen to fit the self-hosted single-process Next.js deployment. Defines tenant-isolation, idempotency, retry, and observability guarantees, and sequences activation of SavedReport.schedule plus proactive AI jobs across all product lenses.
nodes.languageNotes: Evaluates a full options matrix (setInterval, systemd timers, Redis+BullMQ, pg-boss, hand-rolled table) against the single-process self-hosted runtime constraint before recommending pg-boss.

nodes.name: entity-reference-schema.md
nodes.summary: Reuse guide for the shipped entity-reference schema behind universal @-mentions and the Cmd-K palette: a canonical <@type:id> token format across 19 entity types, pure helpers in src/lib/mentions/, a shared Prisma-backed search index (searchEntities/resolveRefs/resolveBacklinks), deep-link URL building, permission scoping, and the polymorphic Reference backlink model. Ends with a checklist for adding a new entity type.
nodes.languageNotes: The token regex is designed for backward compatibility: legacy people-only <@uuid> tokens always resolve to the user type because UUIDs start with a digit and cannot be mistaken for a type prefix.

nodes.name: hr-onboarding-templates.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal for HR onboarding templates built on a lightweight People foundation: Employee/Department models enrich the existing OrgMember rather than building a standalone HRIS, and OnboardingTemplate/OnboardingRun materialize ordered task definitions into real assigned WorkItems on hire. Depends on the work-role ABAC engine for PII sensitivity and the scheduler substrate for overdue reminders.

nodes.name: invoicing-quote-to-cash.md
nodes.summary: Design proposal for native invoicing and quote-to-cash: Invoice/InvoiceLineItem/Payment/InvoiceTemplate Prisma models, an invoice builder that pulls approved billable TimeEntries and reuses the existing pdfkit/DocuSign pipeline, an AI draft_invoice executor, and a build-vs-integrate decision for Zoho Books/QuickBooks import. Names a Float-to-Decimal money migration as a hard prerequisite and gates approval through the shipped ABAC engine.
nodes.languageNotes: Treats money correctness as a gating migration: all existing Float money columns must move to Prisma Decimal (numeric(14,2)) before any invoice math ships.

nodes.name: work-role-abac-engine.md
nodes.summary: As-built documentation of the shipped work-role ABAC engine: WorkRole/OrgMemberWorkRole models layer assignable work roles and a typed JSON deny-rule grammar on top of the existing permission bitfield, evaluated by requireAccess at the single RBAC chokepoint with fail-closed semantics and an OWNER break-glass exemption. The remaining unbuilt piece is AI natural-language policy authoring with pre-save impact simulation.
nodes.languageNotes: v1 is deny-only: allow rules are inert and the engine computes RBAC-baseline AND NOT(any firing deny), deliberately avoiding the footgun where authoring an allow silently revokes the baseline.

nodes.name: audit-integrity.md
nodes.summary: Operator runbook for the tamper-evident audit trail (AU-9 / NIST 800-171 3.3.8): explains the three-layer defense (append-only DB guards, in-DB cryptographic hash-chain with an O(1) chain-head pointer, offsite WORM anchor), how to verify chain integrity via ops one-shot or direct SQL, and the AU-11 retention-purge that preserves tamper-evidence across purge boundaries with signed chain checkpoints.
nodes.languageNotes: Documents a hash-chain design where each audit row binds the previous row's hash, so tampering by a superuser who disables append-only triggers is still detectable in-DB and via offsite WORM diff.

nodes.name: backup-dr.md
nodes.summary: Backup and disaster-recovery runbook (CP-9 / CP-10, NIST 800-171 3.8.9): pgBackRest-to-MinIO encrypted backups, first-run stanza bootstrap, backup schedule, the CP-10 tested restore drill, point-in-time recovery, disaster scenarios, and the single-site DR caveat.

nodes.name: cutover.md
nodes.summary: Per-tenant v1-to-v2 migration runbook driven by the orchestrate.mjs cutover engine: schema-parity gate, read-only export, idempotent owner-mode import, continuous soak-sync while v1 is live, edge write-freeze, final reconcile with never-delete invariants and a delete-count guard, hard verify gate, reverse-proxy flip, finalize, and in-window rollback, with commercial tenants first and gov tenants last.
nodes.languageNotes: The soak-then-reconcile shape shrinks the freeze window to near-zero: watermark deltas drain inserts/updates before the freeze, and only source-side deletes must be applied under freeze via an org-scoped PK-set diff.

nodes.name: observability.md
nodes.summary: Observability runbook (SI-4 / 800-171 3.14.6-3.14.7) for the all-OSS in-boundary monitoring stack: OpenTelemetry app instrumentation exporting OTLP to an OTel Collector fanning out to Prometheus, Jaeger, and Grafana, with the observe-only metric contract, alert first-response steps, and degradation behavior when the collector or classifier is down.
nodes.languageNotes: Telemetry is strictly observe-only and fire-and-forget: instrumentation never alters gate/fail-closed decisions, never emits CUI/PII, and a collector outage can never block the app.

nodes.name: public-hostname-tls.md
nodes.summary: Runbook for the public hostname and TLS front door: the app derives its public origin from X-Forwarded headers set by the bundled Caddy reverse proxy, with two modes (Caddy-terminated auto-HTTPS including an airgapped internal-CA variant, or upstream-terminated TLS behind a proxy/tunnel/LB), OAuth redirect-URI guidance, and the cutover from a Cloudflare tunnel to direct Caddy.

nodes.name: secret-rotation.md
nodes.summary: Secret-rotation runbook (IA-5 / NIST 800-171 3.13.10) covering zero-downtime rotate-then-retire of the vault master key with rollback and compromise procedures, the stateless ANTHROPIC_API_KEY swap, pgBackRest repo-cipher new-stanza rotation, MinIO access-key overlap, forever-retained WORM manifest HMAC keys, database passwords, the one-time legacy Google-token drain-before-drop, and acceptance evidence.

nodes.name: 2026-06-03-classification-phase-1-foundation.md

nodes.languageNotes: Task-by-task executor plan with a locked file structure, verbatim code listings, verification commands, and a self-review checklist per the superpowers planning convention.

nodes.summary: Phase 2 design for the Finance program's bank feeds feature: data model, statement import (2a), and an inbox-plus-reconciliation workflow (2b), with reuse/integration notes, risks, deferred items, and research provenance.

nodes.name: 2026-06-05-ar-invoicing-v1-design.md
nodes.summary: Design for AR/Invoicing v1 (quote-to-cash core): Prisma data model conventions, pure tested money math in src/lib/invoicing/totals.ts, GL posting mappers reusing the ledger's postEntry/safeAutoPost, an org-scoped invoices API guarded by FINANCE_READ/FINANCE_MANAGE, and the finance/invoices UI, sliced into incremental builds.

nodes.name: run-acceptance.sh
nodes.summary: Docker acceptance test for the per-tenant cutover engine: boots two throwaway pgvector Postgres containers, seeds a synthetic org, then proves export -> import -> verify correctness, import idempotency, corruption detection, mutable-row updates, org scoping, and the write-freeze proxy predicate.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a trap-based cleanup handler and PASS/FAIL counters; every external tool (prisma, export/import/verify CLIs) is invoked via npx against host-mapped container ports.

nodes.name: run-cutover-acceptance.sh
nodes.summary: Docker acceptance test for the full cutover flip orchestration: stands up a Caddy reverse proxy, v1/v2 stubs, and four throwaway Postgres instances, then proves pre-flip routing, freeze (405 on writes), flip to v2, unfreeze, other-org isolation, forced-failure rollback to v1, and that the default dry-run touches nothing.
nodes.languageNotes: Drives the TypeScript ProxyControl library through inline `npx tsx -e` snippets and runs everything on a dedicated Docker network so the proxy dials stubs by container name.

nodes.name: run-gov-gate-revoke-acceptance.sh
nodes.summary: Synthetic acceptance test for the two cutover finishers: the gov exposability-map sign-off gate (stable snapshot hash, pass/stale/missing sign-off cases, commercial bypass, orchestrator dry-run blocking) and the provider-side Google token revoke (fake Google, idempotent re-run, dry-run default, org/provider scoping, no token logging).
nodes.languageNotes: Generates a throwaway SSO_VAULT_KEY with openssl to seal seeded credentials, and validates the revoke CLI against a fake Google state file instead of the real provider.

nodes.name: run-parity-acceptance.sh
nodes.summary: Synthetic Docker acceptance test for the cutover schema-parity and provenance hard gate: builds a v2-shaped 'prod' schema dump by construction, then proves the gate passes on a matching dump and fails on two injected drifts (dropped classification FK, dropped table).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses three throwaway Postgres roles — builder, scratch, and shadow — so the parity gate can diff a restored dump against a Prisma-replayed reference schema.

nodes.name: run-snapshot-restore-acceptance.sh
nodes.summary: Docker acceptance test for the pre-flip restore-point capture and validated PITR restore: uses the real pgBackRest stack (custom Postgres image + MinIO S3 repo) to create a named restore point, archive WAL past it, restore a throwaway scratch cluster to the point, and confirm post-capture rows are absent and the orchestrator dry-run plan shows the restore command.
nodes.languageNotes: Executes pgBackRest inside the live compose container via a `docker compose exec` prefix while host-run Node tools connect over a temporarily published port; the only restore target is a throwaway scratch cluster.

nodes.name: run-soak-reconcile-acceptance.sh
nodes.summary: Docker acceptance test for the incremental soak-sync and final reconcile: proves the watermark delta propagates inserts and updates but not deletes, that reconcile-org removes lingering deleted rows under freeze, and that shared closure parents, the other org's rows, and orphan safety are all preserved (including a negative orphaning-delete test).
nodes.languageNotes: Pins known seed UUIDs (global work_item_type, cross-org user) to assert closure-parent invariants after reconcile; runs on ports 55450/55451 to avoid collisions with the other acceptance suites.

nodes.summary: Starts a named throwaway pgvector Postgres container on a given host port and polls until it accepts connections.

nodes.name: report_step
nodes.summary: Asserts that a named orchestration step appears in the captured orchestrator output, recording a PASS or FAIL for the ordered-sequence checks.

nodes.name: start_pg
nodes.summary: Starts a throwaway pgvector Postgres container on the dedicated acceptance Docker network and waits for readiness.

nodes.name: start_pg
nodes.summary: Starts one of the builder/scratch/shadow throwaway pgvector Postgres containers on a given host port and polls until it is ready.

nodes.name: start_pg
nodes.summary: Starts a named throwaway pgvector Postgres container for the soak/reconcile suite and waits until it accepts connections.

nodes.name: build-sign-local.sh
nodes.summary: Offline proof of the CI signed-delivery chain: builds the versioned cosmos-v2 Docker image, generates a real Syft SPDX SBOM, creates a throwaway cosign keypair, pushes to a local registry to obtain a digest, then cosign-signs and verifies by digest. Evidence lands in evidence/local/, covering spec section 8 gates 6 (SBOM) and 7 (sign/provenance).
nodes.languageNotes: Runs every tool (Syft, cosign, registry:2) via Docker so the host needs only docker and node; signs by digest against a throwaway local registry because cosign signatures are OCI artifacts stored next to the image.

nodes.name: restore-drill.sh
nodes.summary: CP-9/CP-10 tested-restore drill: restores the latest pgBackRest backup from the MinIO S3 repo into a scratch Postgres container (never touching the live cluster), starts and promotes it, then runs a verification query with a hard assertion that the audit_logs table (the AU-9 store) survived. Prints RESTORE-DRILL: PASS/FAIL and tears down all scratch resources via an EXIT trap.
nodes.languageNotes: Boots the scratch container with a sleep entrypoint so nothing auto-starts, restores into the empty datadir, then starts Postgres by hand with archive_mode=off so the scratch node never writes to the shared WAL archive repo.

nodes.name: restore-to-point-drill.sh
nodes.summary: Point-in-time restore validation (CP-9/CP-10 and the section 9.4 cutover pre-flip rollback evidence): restores a pgBackRest backup to a named restore point or timestamp in a scratch container, asserts the recovery target was actually reached (cluster promoted out of recovery), and re-runs the base drill's verification query including the audit_logs assertion. Selects the correct base backup by LSN or stop-time so recovery can replay forward to a past target.
nodes.languageNotes: Embeds an inline Node.js script that parses `pgbackrest info --output=json` and compares LSNs with BigInt arithmetic to pick the latest base backup starting at or before the target, avoiding pgBackRest's default-to-latest behavior that would make recovery end before a past target.

nodes.name: run-gates-local.sh
nodes.summary: Offline, record-only run of the security.yml CI gate scanners: Trivy filesystem and image scans, gitleaks full-history secret detection, hadolint Dockerfile lint, and OSV-Scanner on the lockfile, all via their Docker images. Writes JSON reports to evidence/local/ and prints a severity tally, flagging any Critical findings that would fail the real CI gates without failing this local proof.
nodes.languageNotes: Ends with a Node.js heredoc that aggregates all five scanner reports into one severity summary; each scanner is allowed to exit non-zero so a pre-existing finding never aborts the evidence run.

nodes.name: Caddyfile

nodes.languageNotes: Uses Caddy env-var placeholders with defaults ({$VAR:default}) and the TLS-ALPN-01 ACME challenge so inbound port 80 is not required for certificate issuance.
