nodes.name: loadActorPermissions
nodes.summary: Loads the effective permission set for the acting user within the org, backing all executor permission checks.

nodes.name: assertPermission
nodes.summary: Throws a forbidden error unless the actor holds the single required permission, used as the guard at the top of each executor.

nodes.name: loadAuthContext
nodes.summary: Builds the fuller auth context (actor, permissions, membership) that executors needing visibility scoping consume.

nodes.name: assertAllPermissions
nodes.summary: Verifies the actor holds every permission in a required set, throwing on the first missing one.

nodes.name: finance.ts

nodes.name: logExpense
nodes.summary: Creates an expense entry after permission checks with safe auto-posting to the ledger.

nodes.name: getFinanceSummary
nodes.summary: Aggregates non-voided revenue and expense records into a period finance summary using decimal-safe money helpers.

nodes.name: projects.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the project AI executors covering permission enforcement, project matching, and interval lifecycle operations against a mocked Prisma client.

nodes.name: projects.ts
nodes.summary: AI tool executors for project management: list/create/update projects with visibility-scoped access, fuzzy project matching by name or key, and full interval (sprint/PI) lifecycle including creation, update, and completion.

nodes.name: scoreProjectMatch
nodes.summary: Scores how well a project matches a free-text query by comparing key and name tokens, enabling fuzzy project resolution for AI tool calls.

nodes.name: listProjects
nodes.summary: Lists projects the actor may see, applying visibility scoping and optional fuzzy-match filtering by query.

nodes.name: listIntervals
nodes.summary: Lists a project's intervals (sprints/PIs) with status information after resolving the target project.

nodes.name: createInterval
nodes.summary: Creates a new interval for a project, normalizing calendar date inputs to noon-UTC and validating permissions.

nodes.name: createProject
nodes.summary: Creates a project after permission assertion, generating its key and default settings.

nodes.name: updateProject
nodes.summary: Applies partial updates to a project's fields with permission and visibility checks.

nodes.name: updateInterval
nodes.summary: Updates an interval's dates, name, or status with calendar-date normalization and validation.

nodes.name: completeInterval
nodes.summary: Marks an interval complete, handling carry-over of unfinished work and status transitions for contained items.

nodes.name: time-scope.test.ts

nodes.name: time.ts
nodes.summary: AI tool executors for time tracking: log time entries and list entries with per-user visibility scoping, voided-entry exclusion, and rate redaction for actors without rate access.

nodes.name: logTime
nodes.summary: Creates a time entry for the actor (or a permitted target user) after permission assertion.

nodes.name: listTimeEntries
nodes.summary: Lists time entries filtered to the user ids the actor may read, excluding voided entries and redacting rates when the actor lacks rate visibility.

nodes.name: tool-executor.ts
nodes.summary: Central dispatcher for the AI assistant's tool calls: parses tool-call blocks from model output, routes each named tool to the matching domain executor or connector, audits every invocation, and provides composite query/brief helpers.
nodes.languageNotes: Hub module importing every domain executor; dispatchTool is a large switch mapping tool names to executor functions, with connector tools handled through a separate connector registry.

nodes.name: parseToolCalls
nodes.summary: Extracts structured tool calls (name plus JSON arguments) from raw model output, tolerating malformed blocks and returning parse diagnostics.

nodes.name: executeTool
nodes.summary: Public entry point that dispatches a parsed tool call and records an audit trail of the assistant's tool use.

nodes.name: dispatchTool
nodes.summary: Large routing switch mapping every supported tool name (work items, notes, comments, time, finance, accounting, projects, OKRs, PM registers, CRM, compliance, RAG search, connectors, and more) to its executor function.

nodes.name: auditAssistantToolUse
nodes.summary: Writes an audit log record for each assistant tool invocation, summarizing arguments and picking the affected entity id.

nodes.name: queryWorkItems
nodes.summary: Composite helper that queries work items with common filters for assistant summaries.

nodes.name: queryIntervals
nodes.summary: Composite helper returning interval records for assistant reporting.

nodes.name: queryCrm
nodes.summary: Composite helper querying CRM contacts with canonicalized stage filters.

nodes.name: queryFinance
nodes.summary: Composite helper aggregating finance records with money-safe arithmetic for assistant answers.

nodes.name: generateIntervalBrief
nodes.summary: Builds a status brief for an interval by combining its work items and progress data into a summarized structure.

nodes.name: burn.ts
nodes.summary: Computes CLIN burn on read: attributes approved time entries and expenses to each CLIN and rolls up labor/expense actuals against the funded value and ceiling, including a time-phased monthly planned-vs-actual burn series.
nodes.languageNotes: Money math flows through shared Decimal helpers (sumMoney/roundMoney) so rounding matches the payroll and finance modules; values are derived on read and never persisted.

nodes.name: loadClinsWithBurn
nodes.summary: Loads a project's CLINs and computes each one's labor cost (hours priced via entry rate or the employee cost rate), expense cost, total burn, and percent of funded value consumed.

nodes.name: loadClinBurnTimePhased
nodes.summary: Builds a month-by-month burn series across all CLINs: straight-line planned spend over the period of performance versus cumulative actuals, for EVM-style charting.

nodes.name: burn.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the CLIN burn calculations, exercising labor pricing via entry and employee rates, expense attribution, and rounding through the shared money helpers.

nodes.name: export.ts

nodes.name: buildProjectWorkbook
nodes.summary: Fetches all PM register data in parallel and assembles the multi-sheet XLSX workbook, honoring a tracker allowlist and a cost-visibility option that gates staffing cost-rate columns.

nodes.name: export-cost-rate.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests that the staffing sheet in the exported workbook only includes cost-rate data when the caller is permitted to see it, guarding against finance data leaking through exports.

nodes.name: milestone-date.ts
nodes.summary: Pure derivation of a milestone's due date from its linked work items: when autoStatus is set, the due date follows the latest planned end of linked work instead of the stored date.

nodes.summary: Returns the derived due date: the max planned end across linked work items when autoStatus is on and links carry dates, otherwise the stored due date.

nodes.name: dueDateFollowsLinkedWork
nodes.summary: Predicate telling the UI whether a milestone's due date is currently being driven by its linked work (autoStatus on and at least one link).

nodes.name: milestone-date.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for derived milestone due dates, covering autoStatus on/off, missing link dates, and selection of the latest linked planned end.

nodes.name: schedule.ts
nodes.summary: Schedule derivation shared by the milestones API, the Schedule register, and the PM Dashboard: milestone status and completion percentage trickle up from the board columns of linked work items.

nodes.name: deriveMilestone
nodes.summary: Pure derivation of one milestone's status, completion percentage, and at-risk flag from the board columns of its linked work items and the current date.

nodes.name: loadMilestonesWithDerived
nodes.summary: Loads a project's milestones with links, resolves each linked item's board column and due date, and returns milestones enriched with derived status, completion, and due date.

nodes.name: template-export.ts
nodes.summary: Template-based PM export: loads the user's real tracker spreadsheets from templates/ and writes live Cosmos data into cells matched by header text, preserving styles, formulas, data validation, and charts, with formula cells re-emitted so Excel recalculates on open.

nodes.name: loadRegisterRows
nodes.summary: Fetches the rows for a given tracker (risks, changes, blockers, deliverables, schedule, staffing, vendors); staffing deliberately loads with includeCost false so no cost-rate data can leak into the personnel template.

nodes.name: populateRegister
nodes.summary: Writes register rows into a template sheet by mapping header text to columns, preserving per-column formulas by shifting their row references, and seeding ID columns and satellite sheets.

nodes.name: seedVendorLogs
nodes.summary: Seeds the vendor template's Mod Tracker and funding log sheets from contract rows, resolving columns by header and clearing stale data rows first.

nodes.name: seedStaffingSatellites
nodes.summary: Populates the staffing template's satellite compliance sheets (CAC, training, access, NDA) from the loaded staffing rows.

nodes.name: populateBurn
nodes.summary: Fills the burn.xlsx template with live CLIN burn data: monthly actuals priced through the same laborCostFor used by the dashboard, so chart series and dashboard formulas recompute against real numbers.

nodes.name: buildPopulatedTemplate
nodes.summary: Entry point that loads the tracker's template workbook, populates it with live data for the requested tracker, forces recalculation on load, and returns the finished buffer and filename.

nodes.name: forceRecalcOnLoad
nodes.summary: Post-processes the xlsx zip to set the workbook's full-recalc flag so Excel recomputes every formula and chart series the moment the exported file is opened.

nodes.name: approval.ts
nodes.summary: The timesheet approval state machine as pure functions, modeling two approval lanes — labor (hours actually worked) and cost (chargeable to the project/CLIN) — with transitions for submit, approve, withdraw, and reject.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately dependency-free: the machine takes current state and org config and returns the next state, so routes stay thin and the rules are unit-testable without a database.

nodes.name: submitTransition
nodes.summary: Computes the state change when a timesheet is submitted for approval, validating the current status allows submission.

nodes.name: approveTransition
nodes.summary: Computes the state change when one approval lane (labor or cost) signs off, moving to fully approved only when every required lane has signed per the org's requireCostApproval config.

nodes.name: withdrawTransition
nodes.summary: Computes the state change when a submitter withdraws a timesheet, accounting for whether any approval lane has already signed.

nodes.name: rejectTransition
nodes.summary: Computes the state change when an approver rejects a submitted timesheet, returning it to an editable state.

nodes.name: entryStatusFor
nodes.summary: Maps a timesheet status to the TimeEntry.status projection that downstream consumers (CLIN burn, payroll, finance summary) filter on.

nodes.name: approvalAuthority
nodes.summary: Decides whether an actor holds approval authority for a given lane — people managers for the labor lane, project/CLIN owners for the cost lane.

nodes.name: approval.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the timesheet approval state machine covering both approval lanes, submit/approve/withdraw/reject transitions, and single-lane orgs that disable cost approval.

nodes.name: not-voided.ts
nodes.summary: Shared Prisma where-clause (NOT_VOIDED) and helper that every time-entry query must apply to exclude voided (soft-deleted) entries, preventing voided hours from being submitted, approved, or billed against a contract.
nodes.languageNotes: Prisma has no global model filter, so correctness is centralized in one exported constant rather than relying on every call site retyping the filter.

nodes.name: excludeVoided
nodes.summary: Merges the NOT_VOIDED filter into an existing Prisma where clause for time-entry queries.

nodes.name: timesheet-actions.ts
nodes.summary: Applies a timesheet status transition and propagates the projected status to its non-voided time entries in the same database transaction, keeping TimeEntry.status (used by burn, payroll, and finance) consistent with the timesheet; also re-exports org-chart supervisor checks as isManagerOf/hasManager.

nodes.name: applyTimesheetTransition
nodes.summary: Atomically updates a timesheet's status and fans the corresponding entry status out to all its non-voided entries in one transaction, recording the approver and timestamp on the timesheet only.

nodes.name: timesheet-actions.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests for applyTimesheetTransition verifying the timesheet and its entries update atomically, voided entries are left untouched, and entry statuses track the timesheet projection.

nodes.name: item-teams.ts

nodes.name: teamsByUser
nodes.summary: Builds a userId-to-teams lookup from the team list so per-item team resolution is a map hit rather than a scan.

nodes.name: teamLaneFor
nodes.summary: Places an item in exactly one team swimlane based on its assignee's first team, or the unassigned lane.

nodes.name: itemMatchesTeam
nodes.summary: Membership-test filter predicate: does this item's assignee belong to the selected team (an item can match several teams).

nodes.name: item-teams.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for team derivation of work items, covering multi-team members, unassigned items, and the filter-versus-swimlane semantic difference.

nodes.name: team-roster.ts
nodes.summary: Shapes the project Members screen's Teams section: resolves a team's membership (keyed by ProjectMember.id) into displayable rosters and lists members not on any team, kept out of the component so the rules are testable without rendering.

nodes.name: rosterFor
nodes.summary: Resolves a team's member references against the project member list into a sorted, displayable roster with lead flags.

nodes.name: unassignedMembers
nodes.summary: Returns project members (excluding bots) who belong to no team, sorted by name, for the unassigned section of the Teams screen.

nodes.name: team-roster.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for team roster shaping: member resolution, lead flags, bot exclusion, and the unassigned-members list.

nodes.name: activity-label.ts
nodes.summary: Turns raw work-item activity records (field name plus stored value, often a bare id) into human-readable text, resolving id-valued fields to person/interval/type/status names and never surfacing a raw or made-up id — unresolvable ids yield no label at all.

nodes.name: activityFieldLabel
nodes.summary: Maps a raw activity field name (e.g. assigneeId) to a friendly display label (e.g. assignee).

nodes.name: activityValueLabel
nodes.summary: Resolves a raw activity value into readable text via caller-supplied resolvers; returns no label when an id cannot be resolved so the UI degrades to 'changed interval' rather than asserting a wrong value.

nodes.name: activity-label.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for activity label formatting, covering field-name mapping, id resolution through resolvers, and the no-label degradation for unresolvable ids.

nodes.name: estimate-filter.ts
nodes.summary: Board filter that buckets time-tracking estimates (stored in seconds) into working-day size bands (half a day, about a day, most of a week) instead of exposing a numeric comparator.

nodes.name: matchesEstimateBand
nodes.summary: Predicate deciding whether an estimate in seconds falls within the selected size band, including the no-estimate band.

nodes.name: hasAnyEstimate
nodes.summary: Returns whether any item in the list carries an estimate, used to decide if the estimate filter control is worth showing.

nodes.name: estimate-filter.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the estimate size-band filter, exercising band boundaries in hours/days and the no-estimate case.

nodes.name: label-filter.ts
nodes.summary: Label filter for boards using set-intersection semantics (an item has many labels, unlike single-valued type/priority), with OR across the selection so choosing more labels widens the result.

nodes.name: matchesLabelFilter
nodes.summary: Predicate testing whether an item's label set intersects the selected labels; an empty selection is inert and matches everything.

nodes.name: presentLabels
nodes.summary: Collects the distinct labels actually present on the board's items so the filter only offers options that can match something.

nodes.name: label-filter.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the label filter's intersection semantics, inert empty selection, and distinct-label collection.

nodes.name: metadata-filters.ts
nodes.summary: Pure ticket-metadata filter predicates shared by the Kanban and Timeline views: due-date presets (overdue, this week, this month, none) rather than a date picker, plus a generic one-of membership test.

nodes.name: matchesDuePreset
nodes.summary: Predicate deciding whether a due date satisfies the selected preset (any, overdue, due this week, due this month, no due date) relative to a supplied now.

nodes.name: matchesOneOf
nodes.summary: Generic one-of predicate for single-valued fields (type, priority, interval): matches when the value is in the selection or the selection is empty.

nodes.name: metadata-filters.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the due-date preset and one-of predicates, pinning week/month boundaries against a fixed clock.

nodes.name: relation-filters.ts
nodes.summary: Board lenses that need a relation rather than an item field — blocked-ness from work-item links, milestone membership from milestone links, and story-point filtering — each resolved once into a Set so a 500-item board stays linear instead of quadratic.

nodes.name: blockedItemIds
nodes.summary: Resolves the set of item ids that are targets of blocking links, computed once per board render.

nodes.name: matchesBlocked
nodes.summary: Predicate testing an item against the blocked/unblocked/any filter using the precomputed blocked-id set.

nodes.name: milestoneItemIds
nodes.summary: Builds a milestone-id to linked-work-item-id-set index from milestone link rows.

nodes.name: matchesMilestone
nodes.summary: Predicate testing whether an item is linked to the selected milestone using the precomputed index.

nodes.name: presentStoryPoints
nodes.summary: Collects the distinct story-point values present on the board's items (including the no-estimate sentinel) to populate the filter's options.

nodes.name: matchesStoryPoints
nodes.summary: Predicate testing an item's story points against the selected values, treating the NO_ESTIMATE sentinel as matching items without points.

nodes.name: relation-filters.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the relation-based board filters: blocking-link resolution, milestone membership indexing, and story-point matching including the no-estimate sentinel.

nodes.name: models.ts
nodes.summary: Central client-side type definitions: 51 exported interfaces and type aliases covering the whole domain — projects, boards, work items, intervals, OKRs, CRM, notes, notifications, contracts, custom fields, time entries, finance, meetings, integrations, webhooks, compliance, security settings, and assistant conversations — consumed by nearly every dashboard component.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure ambient shape declarations with string dates (API JSON shapes) rather than Prisma model types, decoupling the client from the database schema.

Idempotent and slug-keyed; never deletes existing data.
nodes.languageNotes: Loads DATABASE_URL from .env.local itself and is deliberately NOT wired into npm run seed; every write is upserted or sentinel-guarded.

nodes.name: loadEnv
nodes.summary: Parses .env.local by hand to extract DATABASE_URL without printing secrets, so the seed can run standalone outside the Next.js env loader.

nodes.name: findOrCreateUser
nodes.summary: Looks up a user by email and creates it with a display name and options if missing, keeping the seed idempotent across re-runs.

nodes.name: ensureNamedChannel
nodes.summary: Finds or creates a named chat channel (slug, name, topic) for an org, returning its id without duplicating on re-run.

nodes.name: ensureGeneralChannel
nodes.summary: Ensures the org has a #general chat channel, creating it under the given creator user if absent.

nodes.languageNotes: Run after demo-defense.ts; looks the org up by slug and only adds what is missing.

nodes.name: loadEnv
nodes.summary: Reads DATABASE_URL out of .env.local by parsing the file directly, allowing the seed to run without any framework env loading.

nodes.summary: Runs every enrichment section for the Apex demo org — sprints, backlog, time entries, BD pipeline, meetings, OKRs, finance, NIST controls — each inside a guarded section() wrapper.

nodes.summary: Layer-3 'fill every page' demo seed that deepens Apex Defense so every COSMOS v2 page has believable content: full accounting suite, invoices/AR, banking, payroll, tax, delivery goals/KPIs, analytics, roles, security, integrations, agent governance, feedback, and documents. Count-guarded or upserted per domain so re-runs only add what is missing.
nodes.languageNotes: Depends on the org, users, project, sprints, and partners created by demo-defense.ts and demo-defense-extra.ts, but seeds its own chart of accounts.

nodes.name: loadEnv
nodes.summary: Parses .env.local for DATABASE_URL so the standalone seed can connect to the tenant database.

nodes.languageNotes: Reuses the production risk scoring (computeRiskScore / riskLevelFromScore) so seeded risk levels match what the app would compute.

nodes.name: main

nodes.name: demo-defense-roadmap.ts

nodes.name: roadmap-import.ts
nodes.summary: Generic CLI roadmap loader that installs a roadmap node set into one project: --demo loads the committed mock, or --org/--project/--file load gitignored real-program JSON. Idempotent — re-running replaces (default) or merges the project's roadmap.

nodes.name: loadEnvLocal

nodes.name: toImportNode
nodes.summary: Normalizes a raw JSON record into a RoadmapImportNode, splitting known core keys from extra metadata fields.

nodes.name: ensureGeneralChannel
nodes.summary: Ensures the test org has a #general chat channel, creating it if missing and returning its id.

nodes.name: autoJoinGeneral
nodes.summary: Upserts a channel membership so a given user is joined to the org's #general channel, optionally as admin.

nodes.name: ensureProjectFixture
nodes.summary: Creates the test project with its default board, columns, and Alice as project member inside a single transaction, skipping when it already exists.

nodes.summary: Ensures the built-in Task work-item type exists so specs can create work items against it.

nodes.summary: Upserts employee records forming a small org chart (alice, bob, carol) for the test organization.

nodes.summary: Orchestrates the fixture seed: creates the test org and users, joins channels, and runs every ensure* helper in order.

nodes.name: wire-keycloak-idp.ts
nodes.summary: Operational script that attaches or updates a Keycloak OIDC IdpConnection on an existing org, sealing the client secret with the crypto/vault keyring before it touches the database. Fully parameterized via environment variables and idempotent via upsert on orgId.
nodes.languageNotes: The plaintext client secret never lands in a DB column — it is sealed under SSO_VAULT_KEYS/SSO_VAULT_KEY before the upsert, so re-running rotates the secret in place.

nodes.name: resolveDbUrl
nodes.summary: Resolves DATABASE_URL from the environment or .env.local so the script can run against a deployed database.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Looks up the target org, seals the Keycloak client secret via sealSecret, and upserts the org's single IdpConnection with issuer, scopes, and the encrypted secret.

nodes.name: work-item-fields.ts
nodes.summary: Client-safe shared contract for the work-item importer: defines the target-field catalog (TARGET_FIELDS), ignore list, and heuristics that map arbitrary Jira/Linear/CSV columns onto the WorkItem model, including header guessing, priority normalization, and Jira-style duration parsing.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately has no server-only imports so both the client wizard and the server import engine can share the same mapping contract.

nodes.name: guessTarget
nodes.summary: Guesses which target WorkItem field a source column header maps to by normalized header lookup.

nodes.name: guessPriority
nodes.summary: Normalizes free-form priority strings (p0/urgent/sev1, high/major, low/minor, etc.) onto the Priority enum via regex buckets.

nodes.name: parseDurationSeconds
nodes.summary: Parses raw duration values — plain integer seconds or Jira-style '2w 3d 4h 5m' strings — into whole seconds, returning null for unparseable input.

nodes.name: types.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the roadmap ingest contract, validating roadmapImportSchema/roadmapImportNodeSchema acceptance and rejection cases.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Roadmap ingest contract: zod schemas (roadmapImportNodeSchema, roadmapImportSchema) and the ROADMAP_NODE_KINDS list describing a project's roadmap tree. Kept deliberately LLM-friendly — only kind and title are required; anchors, sortOrder, and ids are derived server-side.
nodes.languageNotes: Intentionally has no MILESTONE kind — milestones live solely in the Milestone table so the word means one thing across boards.

nodes.name: merge-deps.mjs
nodes.summary: Merges plugin-declared npm dependencies from plugin.json into core's dependencies map for the composed build. Version conflicts are fatal by design — a composed image installs exactly one version of each package, so silent resolution would ship something the plugin author never tested.

nodes.name: mergeDependencies
nodes.summary: Merges each plugin's dependencies into a copy of core's dependency map, throwing on any version conflict and returning a key-sorted result for stable diffs.

nodes.name: merge-deps.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for mergeDependencies covering merge behavior, conflict detection between core and plugins, and stable key ordering.

nodes.name: render-registry.mjs
nodes.summary: Code generators that render the plugin registry source files: renderRegistryIndex emits the client-safe manifest registrations and renderRegistryServer emits server-hook plus integration-provider registrations for composed plugins.

nodes.name: renderRegistryIndex
nodes.summary: Renders src/lib/plugins/registry/index.ts source: manifest imports plus PluginRegistry.register calls for each composed plugin entry.

nodes.name: renderRegistryServer
nodes.summary: Renders src/lib/plugins/registry/server.ts source: server-hook imports, PluginServerRegistry registrations, and IntegrationRegistry registration of each hook's integrations.

nodes.name: render-registry.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the registry renderers, asserting that emitted import identifiers, register calls, and integration loops use consistently camelized slugs.

nodes.name: slug.mjs
nodes.summary: Build-side slug helper exporting camelSlug, which converts a kebab-case plugin slug into the camelCase identifier prefix used in generated registry code.

nodes.name: camelSlug
nodes.summary: Converts a kebab-case slug to camelCase by uppercasing each character following a hyphen.

nodes.name: slug.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests asserting camelSlug's kebab-to-camel conversion and its agreement with the runtime pluginModelPrefix in src/lib/plugins/slug.ts, so build-time and runtime slug camelization can never drift apart.

nodes.name: sync.mjs
nodes.summary: Plugin composition tool (ADR 0003): overlays private plugin repos from plugins/<slug>/ into the cosmos-v2 tree at build time — copying overlays, appending Prisma schema fragments and back-relations at marker comments, merging plugin dependencies into package.json, and regenerating the plugin registries. Every written path is added to .git/info/exclude so plugin code can never be committed to the public core; --clean reverses everything.
nodes.languageNotes: Tracks composed files with content hashes and a dirty-composed guard so local edits to composed output are detected before being clobbered or restored.

nodes.name: guardDirtyComposed
nodes.summary: Compares recorded content hashes of previously composed files against the working tree and aborts if any composed file was hand-edited, preventing silent loss of local changes.

nodes.name: removeManagedExclude
nodes.summary: Strips the managed plugin-sync block from .git/info/exclude so a clean run leaves no stale exclusion entries.

nodes.name: restore
nodes.summary: Implements --clean: removes composed overlay files, restores modified tracked files (package.json, schema, registries) from git, and clears the managed exclude entries and hash ledger.

nodes.name: plugin-isolation.arch.test.ts
nodes.summary: Architecture test enforcing ADR 0003 plugin isolation: shared code may only reach into plugins through the two registry files and (plugin-<slug>) route shims, and must never query plugin-owned Prisma model accessors directly (matched via pluginModelPrefix).

nodes.name: slug.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for pluginModelPrefix, verifying kebab-case slugs camelize into valid Prisma client accessor prefixes.

nodes.name: slug.ts
nodes.summary: Runtime slug helper exporting pluginModelPrefix, which camelizes a kebab-case plugin slug into the Prisma client accessor prefix. Anything matching plugin-owned model accessors by slug must go through this — building prisma.${slug} directly can never match a real accessor for hyphenated slugs.
nodes.languageNotes: Exists because the isolation guard once passed vacuously for hyphenated slugs when raw slugs were used to match camelCased Prisma accessors.

nodes.name: pluginModelPrefix
nodes.summary: Converts a kebab-case plugin slug into the camelCase prefix of its generated Prisma client model accessors.

nodes.name: project.ts
nodes.summary: List-projection for the cross-project work-item query: defines the serialisable IssueRow shape for the org-wide Issues list and runWorkItemQuery, which executes the RBAC-scoped query and batch-resolves project keys, type labels, assignee display names, and parent labels.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately never includes OrgMember.permissions (a BigInt) — the only serialised user fields are id, displayName, and avatarUrl, keeping every row JSON-safe.

nodes.name: runWorkItemQuery
nodes.summary: Builds the Prisma where/orderBy via buildWorkItemWhere and buildOrderBy, runs findMany plus count in parallel, then batch-fetches referenced projects, assignees, and parents to assemble fully-resolved IssueRow results with a total count.

nodes.name: date-only.ts
nodes.summary: Timezone-safe handling of date-ONLY values: dateOnlyKey extracts the YYYY-MM-DD prefix from Prisma's UTC-midnight serialisation of Postgres DATE columns, and byDateOnlyDesc sorts by it, so a calendar day is never shifted by the viewer's timezone.
nodes.languageNotes: Fixes a production bug where the timesheet list showed 7/19 for an entry the week grid drew on 7/20 — the rule is to take the YYYY-MM-DD prefix and never construct a Date from the full instant.

nodes.name: dateOnlyKey
nodes.summary: Returns the YYYY-MM-DD prefix of a date-only value, avoiding any timezone conversion.

nodes.name: byDateOnlyDesc
nodes.summary: Comparator sorting records newest-first by their date-only key using string comparison.

nodes.name: date-only.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the date-only helpers, verifying prefix extraction, descending sort order, and agreement with the stable date formatters across timezone-hostile inputs.

nodes.name: period.ts
nodes.summary: Pay-period math on YYYY-MM-DD strings and UTC-constructed dates: periodFor resolves the WEEKLY, BIWEEKLY, or SEMIMONTHLY period a given day belongs to, and samePeriod compares two days. Periods are resolved per entry so a week spanning the 15th splits correctly across two semi-monthly periods.
nodes.languageNotes: All arithmetic is UTC-only; a boundary computed in the viewer's zone would bill an entry to the wrong pay period.

nodes.name: periodFor
nodes.summary: Computes the inclusive start and end (YYYY-MM-DD) of the weekly, biweekly, or semi-monthly period containing a given day, using Monday-based UTC arithmetic.

nodes.name: samePeriod
nodes.summary: Returns whether two date-only values fall in the same pay period for a given period length.

nodes.name: period.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for pay-period resolution covering weekly, biweekly, and semi-monthly boundaries, month edges, and samePeriod comparisons.

nodes.name: timesheet.ts
nodes.summary: Lazy timesheet provisioning: timesheetIdForEntry upserts the pay-period timesheet a time entry belongs to on first use, and isTimesheetOpen checks whether a timesheet still accepts edits. Period length is a parameter because it becomes per-org policy in a later slice.
nodes.languageNotes: Timesheets are created on demand rather than provisioned per user per week, avoiding a table that grows without anyone asking for it; the WEEKLY default matches the ISO Monday-based backfill.

nodes.name: timesheetIdForEntry
nodes.summary: Resolves the pay period for an entry date via periodFor and upserts the corresponding Timesheet row, returning its id.

nodes.name: isTimesheetOpen
nodes.summary: Returns whether a timesheet is still editable by checking its status against the closed-status list.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Four-stage Docker build (deps, build, migrate, runtime) producing the Node 24 production image for cosmos-v2 on port 3000, plus a migrate stage for running Prisma migrations. Bakes the MiniLM ONNX embeddings model into node_modules at build time so gov deployments never fetch at runtime, with retry/backoff and optional HF_TOKEN authentication for the flaky HuggingFace download.
nodes.languageNotes: The model download layer sits before COPY . . so pure code changes reuse the cached layer; a package.json version bump intentionally busts it.

nodes.name: deps
nodes.summary: Dependency stage: copies package.json and package-lock.json and runs npm ci on node:24-bookworm-slim to produce a cacheable node_modules layer.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Build stage: reuses deps' node_modules, bakes the MiniLM embeddings model for offline runtime use (with retries and optional hf_token secret), copies the source, and compiles the Next.js application with a raised heap limit.

nodes.name: migrate
nodes.summary: Migration stage derived from the build stage, used to run Prisma database migrations against the target environment before the runtime image starts.

nodes.name: runtime
nodes.summary: Minimal production runtime stage on node:24-bookworm-slim exposing port 3000, carrying only the built app and the assets needed to serve cosmos-v2.

nodes.name: auto-tag-release.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that automatically creates a git tag when the version changes on a push to main, which in turn kicks off the release pipeline.

nodes.name: ci.yml

nodes.name: feedback-remediation-pr.yml

nodes.name: feedback-remediation.yml

nodes.name: release.yml

nodes.languageNotes: Assembly builds compose private plugin checkouts pinned by plugins.lock.json so released images are reproducible.

nodes.name: security.yml

nodes.name: 2026-07-26-pi-planning-plugin-design.md

nodes.summary: Audit of the access-control model across tenant, org, and project layers: what is enforced (org/project admin boundary, ABAC, multi-tenancy), what is not (ProjectMember as read boundary), a bypassable in_project deny finding, and shipped remediations.

nodes.name: autonomous-delivery.md
nodes.summary: Operational runbook for the Foreman autonomous delivery daemon: the pick-build-verify loop, operator controls, the audit trail for reworking or rolling back changes, safety rails, and troubleshooting steps.

nodes.name: feedback-remediation.md
nodes.summary: Runbook for the feedback auto-remediation loop: what the loop does, in-app configuration, activating the scheduled poller workflow, optionally drafting fixes as PRs, and the guardrails that bound it.

nodes.name: 2026-06-03-classification-phase-4-chat-attachments.md
nodes.summary: Carried-over v1 implementation plan for Classification Phase 4: adding classificationLevel to ChatMessageAttachment via schema migration, classifying attachments on send, carrying the level through history/replies selects, and rendering a chip in the attachment tile.

nodes.name: 2026-06-04-classification-phase-5-documents-module.md
nodes.summary: Carried-over v1 implementation plan for Classification Phase 5, the Documents/Files module: Document model and migration, DOCUMENT_READ/WRITE permissions, cappedLevel policy helper, list/upload/serve/reclassify routes, and the documents tab UI.

nodes.name: 2026-06-03-classification-propagation-design.md
nodes.summary: Carried-over v1 design spec for classification propagation: a core src/lib/classification library (ranking, effective ceiling, banner formatting), schema changes, five delivery phases from foundation to a Documents module, and ABAC/audit considerations.

nodes.name: dependabot.yml
nodes.summary: Dependabot configuration scheduling automated dependency updates across three ecosystems: npm packages, GitHub Actions workflow pins, and Docker base images.

nodes.name: pre-commit
nodes.summary: Husky pre-commit hook that blocks commits containing merge-conflict markers and then runs lint-staged formatters/linters on staged files.

nodes.name: .trivyignore
nodes.summary: Accepted-risk register for the Trivy vulnerability gates: suppresses five CRITICAL CVEs (mostly perl-base and zlib1g base-image packages) that have no upstream fix, each documented as a NIST 800-171 POA&M item.
nodes.languageNotes: Only unfixable CRITICALs are suppressed; fixable ones are remediated by rebuilding on a patched base image rather than being listed here.

nodes.name: uds-rke2-setup.md
nodes.summary: End-to-end guide for deploying COSMOS on RKE2 with UDS Core: platform bring-up (storage, MetalLB), Helm chart scaffold, MinIO, CrunchyData Postgres with pgvector, SOPS secrets, migrate hooks, gateway exposure, airgap packaging, and a troubleshooting playbook.
nodes.languageNotes: Catalogs the k3d-to-RKE2/UDS migration gotchas explicitly, including the local-path vs UDS storage conflicts.

nodes.name: eslint.config.mjs
nodes.summary: ESLint flat config layering Next.js presets with custom architectural guards: a ban on silent console.error-only catch blocks, a single-path AI egress rule restricting direct provider imports, and ADR 0003 plugin-isolation import restrictions.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses no-restricted-syntax/no-restricted-imports as the editor-time half of invariants whose test half lives in arch tests; notes that flat-config same-rule options replace rather than merge.

nodes.name: prisma.config.ts
nodes.summary: Prisma 7 CLI/Migrate configuration supplying the datasource URL (with a placeholder fallback so schema-engine commands never silently fail), migrations path, and seed command; the application runtime bypasses it via the pg driver adapter.
nodes.languageNotes: A literal unroutable placeholder URL avoids both the eager env() throw and the schema-engine's refusal to start without a datasource argument.

nodes.name: org_entitlements
nodes.summary: Hand-written, idempotent migration creating the per-tenant org_entitlements table (1:1 with organizations, cascade-delete) that gates which product modules and industry sectors an org sees via tri-state allowlist flags plus arrays; a missing row means everything enabled.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses IF NOT EXISTS and a pg_constraint existence check so re-applied deploys are no-ops; the flag-plus-array pair stands in for a nullable scalar list, which Prisma cannot model.

nodes.name: 20260728010000_refresh_software_template
nodes.summary: Deploy-time repair that brings the built-in Software Project template up to the current seed: renames the 'Sprint Dashboard' board template to 'Sprint Health' and fixes the template's enabledFeatures (replacing the dead 'risk' key and adding the missing 'interval' key that made the Intervals button disappear).
nodes.languageNotes: A migration rather than a seed change because seeds only run at bootstrap while `prisma migrate deploy` runs on every deploy; scoped to org_id IS NULL AND is_built_in so tenant-customized templates are untouched.

nodes.name: 20260728020000_rename_existing_sprint_dashboards
nodes.summary: Backfill companion to the template refresh: renames DASHBOARD boards still literally named 'Sprint Dashboard' to 'Sprint Health' on projects already created from the built-in software template, leaving user-renamed boards and other sectors alone.

nodes.name: 20260728030000_standalone_labels
nodes.summary: Promotes labels from bare strings in work_items.tags to first-class rows: creates org-scoped `labels` and the `work_item_labels` join table with case-insensitive uniqueness, while deliberately keeping the tags array populated so RAID, AI tools, ingest and feedback paths need no cutover.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirror-instead-of-cutover strategy: both the new tables and the legacy tags array stay in step via a single application-side helper.

nodes.name: labels
nodes.summary: Org-scoped label catalog (id, org_id, name, color) with a case-insensitive unique name per org, giving each organization a single renamable, recolorable list of labels.

nodes.name: work_item_labels
nodes.summary: Join table associating work items with label rows, unique per (work_item_id, label_id) and indexed by org and label for cross-project label queries.

nodes.name: 20260728040000_backfill_software_project_features
nodes.summary: Backfills the full feature set onto projects created from the broken software template — rows still holding the never-valid 'risk' key and lacking 'interval' — restoring the unreachable Intervals button; the 'risk' key proves the row was never edited in settings, making the overwrite safe.

nodes.name: 20260729120000_convert_milestone_typed_work_items
nodes.summary: Data migration that materializes real `milestones` rows for work items filed under the shadow 'Milestone' work-item type (cross.milestone), keeping the originating work item and linking the pair through milestone_links with auto_status so the milestone's status derives from the ticket.
nodes.languageNotes: Reversible by design: only milestones and milestone_links rows are written, so undo is a DELETE; the source work item keeps its ticket number, comments, and audit trail.

nodes.name: 20260729140000_fix_sector_template_dead_features
nodes.summary: Fixes dead feature keys ('risk', 'decision', 'meeting_note') in the six remaining built-in sector templates (aec, consulting, manufacturing, ops, education, event) and repairs projects already created from them, adding the missing 'interval' key and per-sector pm-dashboard/risk-register decisions.

nodes.name: 20260729140000_objective_interval_and_committed
nodes.summary: Adds SAFe PI Objective support to `objectives`: an `interval_id` timebox reference (ON DELETE SET NULL so deleting a PI orphans rather than destroys its objectives) and a `committed` boolean defaulting true to distinguish committed from stretch objectives.

nodes.name: 20260729160000_teams_and_scoped_project_access
nodes.summary: Introduces teams as a first-class core concept (`teams` and `team_members` tables) plus an opt-in `team_scoped_access` flag on projects; the flag defaults to false so no existing org loses project visibility, and the PI Planning plugin maps onto these teams instead of keeping its own registry.
nodes.languageNotes: Opt-in narrowing pattern: read scoping only activates per project when explicitly enabled, because project_members was never maintained as an access list.

nodes.name: teams
nodes.summary: Project-scoped team roster (org_id, project_id, name) with unique team names per project, forming the org → projects → teams → members hierarchy.

nodes.name: team_members
nodes.summary: Membership join table tying a project member to a team, unique per (team_id, project_member_id).

nodes.name: 20260730130000_objective_links_and_link_type_defaults
nodes.summary: Purely additive change letting objectives link directly to delivery work items via a new `objective_links` table, plus nullable per-project columns choosing which work-item type link pickers offer first; existing key_result_links and objective laddering are untouched.

nodes.name: objective_links
nodes.summary: Association table mapping an objective to a work item (unique per pair), shaped like key_result_links but without a type column since the work item already knows its type.

nodes.name: 20260730190000_board_team_scoping
nodes.summary: Adds a nullable `team_id` to boards so a board can belong to a team within its project; null means project-shared (today's behavior), and ON DELETE SET NULL makes deleted teams release their boards back to the project instead of destroying or hiding them.
nodes.languageNotes: The (project_id, team_id) composite index matches the always-paired filter 'team_id IS NULL OR team_id = ANY(my teams)' within a project.

nodes.name: 20260730220000_drop_duplicate_milestone_type
nodes.summary: Deletes the duplicate 'Milestone' work-item type (consulting.milestone_item) that shadowed cross.milestone in the Issues type filter, guarded so the delete only fires when no work item references the type.

nodes.name: 20260731120000_employee_manager
nodes.summary: Adds a nullable self-referencing `manager_id` to employees — the org chart's first edge — so supervisors can see the time entries they approve after time reads were pinned to the actor; no backfill, so the migration cannot widen anyone's access on its own.

nodes.name: 20260731170000_timesheet_audit_spine
nodes.summary: Builds the audit spine for timekeeping: pay-period `timesheets` with a status workflow, append-only `time_entry_revisions` recording before/after values, and void-instead-of-delete columns on time entries — turning time data into audit-admissible evidence via an entirely additive change.
nodes.languageNotes: Append-only revision history distinguishes 'never entered' from 'removed after the fact', which hard deletes make impossible for an auditor.

nodes.name: timesheets
nodes.summary: Per-user pay-period record with a TimesheetStatus workflow (OPEN → SUBMITTED → LABOR_APPROVED → APPROVED / REJECTED / LOCKED), dual labor/cost approval stamps, and attestation timestamp; unique per (org, user, period_start).

nodes.name: time_entry_revisions
nodes.summary: Append-only audit log of time-entry changes capturing previous and changed values, the reason, the acting user and their IP.

nodes.name: 20260801120000_scope_builtin_project_manager
nodes.summary: Re-syncs the built-in 'Project Manager' work role's permission mask to the narrowed catalog value at deploy time, removing 11 org-wide admin bits (PROJECT_MANAGE, BOARD_MANAGE, etc.) that made every Project Manager an administrator of every project in the org.
nodes.languageNotes: The grants literal is permissionMaskFromKeys serialized by maskToDb; builtin-work-roles.test.ts recomputes it from the catalog so the two cannot silently drift.

nodes.name: 20260801190000_timesheet_approver
nodes.summary: Adds an `approver_ids` UUID array to timesheets recording who a submitted sheet was routed to, with a GIN index serving the 'sheets routed to me' containment query; deliberately not backfilled so pre-routing rows honestly read as 'nobody was asked'.
nodes.languageNotes: GIN index because the approvals-queue query is array containment (approver_ids @> ARRAY[me]), which a B-tree cannot answer.

nodes.name: 20260801200000_employee_supervisors
nodes.summary: Turns the org chart into a graph: a new `employee_supervisors` table lets an employee have several supervisors (matrixed orgs, deputies), superseding and backfilling from the single employees.manager_id column, which is kept unread for one release to preserve rollback.

nodes.name: employee_supervisors
nodes.summary: Many-to-many supervision edge (employee_id, supervisor_id, created_by_id) unique per pair, cascading on both sides so departures leave reports visibly unsupervised rather than pointing at ghosts.

nodes.name: 20260801220000_project_manager_loses_time_approve
nodes.summary: Removes TIME_APPROVE from the built-in 'Project Manager' work role at deploy time, separating delivery management from payroll sign-off; approval authority moves to the worker's supervisors or the 'Reviewer / Approver' role, with deliberate non-auto-granting so each org chooses its approvers.

nodes.name: 20260802140000_supervisor_requests
nodes.summary: Creates `supervisor_requests`, the escape hatch from the 'no supervisor, cannot submit a timesheet' block: a worker names a desired supervisor and a permission-holder performs the assignment; a row is an open request (no status column) and honouring or declining it deletes the row, making the unique pair index a spam guard by construction.
nodes.languageNotes: Request-not-self-service by design: letting the subject assign their own approver would defeat the control the approval workflow exists to provide; the audit log is the permanent record.

nodes.name: supervisor_requests
nodes.summary: Open supervisor-assignment requests (employee_id, supervisor_id, requested_by_id), unique per pair and cascading on both sides so departing workers or approvers leave no dangling rows.

nodes.name: schema.prisma
nodes.summary: The master Prisma schema for the entire multi-tenant platform: 4,100+ lines defining the PostgreSQL data model — orgs, plans and GOV/COMMERCIAL tenant classes, projects, boards (13 board types from KANBAN to PROGRAM), work items, OKRs, teams, timesheets, RBAC roles, and the rest of the PM/finance/compliance domain — from which the Prisma client is generated.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the postgresqlExtensions preview feature with pgcrypto (gen_random_uuid), and carries @plugin markers so plugin schema fragments can be composed into it at build time.

nodes.name: check-conflict-markers.mjs
nodes.summary: Pre-commit guard that refuses to commit unresolved merge-conflict markers: scans the STAGED blob content (not the working tree) of every added/changed file for line-anchored <<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>> markers, skipping binaries, and exits 1 listing offenders.
nodes.languageNotes: Reads staged blobs via `git show :<file>` because staged and working-tree content deliberately differ here (release:bump leaves them disagreeing); markers are anchored to line starts to avoid false positives on regexes and docs.

nodes.name: bump-version.mjs
nodes.summary: Release version bumper for the plugin-composed working tree, replacing `npm version` which silently fails here: it reconstructs package.json/package-lock.json from git HEAD, writes only the version field, refuses to stage anything beyond the version (so composed plugin dependencies never leak into the neutral public core), then restores the composed tree and skip-worktree flags.
nodes.languageNotes: Works around sync.mjs marking composed files skip-worktree: `npm version` would edit them, `git add -A` would ignore them, and the release would ship under the old number with no error.

nodes.name: gen-migration.mjs
nodes.summary: Generates the additive SQL migration for the currently-composed plugins (ADR 0003: plugins do not ship migrations): diffs the neutral schema at git HEAD against the composed schema on disk via `prisma migrate diff --script`, a purely textual operation that never opens a database connection, and writes the SQL to a file for review and normal deploy-pipeline application.
nodes.languageNotes: The output is always a plugin's ENTIRE schema, not a delta — its comments warn that overwriting an already-shipped init migration with it is how a live instance once lost 11 of 13 plugin tables, because `prisma migrate deploy` skips recorded migrations without re-reading the file.

nodes.name: lock.mjs
nodes.summary: Maintains plugins.lock.json, which records the exact plugin commit each core release composes with so builds are reproducible: default mode reports drift between the lockfile and the checked-out plugin HEADs (exit 1 on any), --write records current HEADs; refs are constrained to a full SHA or literal 'main' to block ref injection.
nodes.languageNotes: Only a commit SHA and slug are recorded, disclosing nothing about a private plugin repo's contents; readJson parses-and-catches instead of existsSync-then-read to avoid the CodeQL file-system race.

nodes.name: headOf
nodes.summary: Resolves the git HEAD SHA of a plugin directory, first confirming via rev-parse --show-toplevel that the directory is its own repository root rather than a subdirectory of the core repo.

nodes.name: lock.test.ts
nodes.summary: Shape guard for plugins.lock.json: asserts the lockfile exists (without it the assembly build silently falls back to plugin main), pins at least one plugin, uses only full-SHA or 'main' refs (blocking ref-injection vectors like refs/pull/1/head), and uses kebab-case slugs that cannot smuggle a path.

nodes.name: sync.integration.test.ts
nodes.summary: End-to-end exercise of the plugin composition script (sync.mjs) against a synthetic plugin in a throwaway git sandbox — the orchestration layer previously ran only in developer terminals and release builds, which is how an untested dependency-merging branch exited 127 on a GitHub runner and stopped the v2.240.0 image from building.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs in a mkdtemp copy of the repo because sync.mjs writes into src/, edits package.json, and sets skip-worktree — destructive against a real working tree.

nodes.name: buildSandbox
nodes.summary: Constructs the minimal throwaway repository sync.mjs needs — a git-initialized temp dir with a marker-carrying schema.prisma, package.json/lock, the sync script itself, and a synthetic plugin declaring schema fragments and npm dependencies — and commits it so skip-worktree manipulation works.

nodes.name: assistant-prompt.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for Cosmo's system-prompt builder: verifies the identity block names the requesting user (name, id, role), falls back to the user id when the name is blank, keeps email out of the injected block to match the GOV-mode PII posture, and includes the dated 'now' block.

nodes.name: assistant-prompt.ts
nodes.summary: Builds the system prompt for Cosmo, the platform's agentic AI assistant: a static base covering identity, operating rules, Foreman routing, and behavior under the CUI-blind egress gate, composed per-request with a dated US-Eastern 'now' block and an identity block naming the authenticated user (name, id, role — deliberately never email).
nodes.languageNotes: Kept out of the API route so it is unit-testable without next/server; capability details defer to the live tool list so the prompt cannot fossilize a hardcoded feature menu.

nodes.name: buildNowBlock
nodes.summary: Renders the current date/time as a prompt block in US Eastern with an explicit YYYY-MM-DD (via the en-CA locale trick), anchoring the model's relative-date math so 'tomorrow' stops landing weeks off in the wrong year.

nodes.name: buildAssistantSystemPrompt
nodes.summary: Composes Cosmo's full per-request system prompt — base + now block + an identity block telling the model exactly who it is talking to, so 'me'/'assign to me' resolves to the requesting user's id without asking.

nodes.name: time-read-gate.arch.test.ts
nodes.summary: Grep-based architecture test asserting the time-read rule across EVERY consumer of the timeEntry table — routes and AI tools alike must scope reads through readableTimeUserIds and redact rates via redactRates — after the AI chat tool kept returning the whole org's hours and rates when only the REST route was fixed.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately crude source-scanning: the only kind of test that fails for a NEW reader nobody thought to test, which is how the same shared-rule bug shipped three times (voidedAt, laborCostFor, and this).

nodes.name: route-project.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for projectKeyFromRoute: extracts the project key from '/org/projects/KEY/...' paths, returns null when no project segment exists (settings pages, root, undefined), and ignores query strings, hashes, and trailing slashes.

nodes.name: ssr-safe-dates.arch.test.ts
nodes.summary: Source-level architecture test forbidding runtime-locale toLocaleDateString() calls in SSR-rendered components, which made server and browser render different text for the same instant and surfaced as React hydration error #418 ('Something went wrong' toast); enforces a per-file allowlist of files converted to formatDateStable rather than a blanket ban.
nodes.languageNotes: A per-file allowlist is deliberate: chart axes built from local date arithmetic would shift a day if pinned to UTC, and tooltips/dialog bodies never render during SSR — so blanket conversion would break real behavior. Unit tests cannot catch this class of bug because Testing Library renders client-only.

nodes.name: branch-options.arch.test.ts
nodes.summary: Architecture test asserting every PM-register component labels its branch picker through the branchOptions helper rather than interpolating code and name itself — each register renders the picker twice (inline-edit and create dialog), and only half were converted, so production offered doubled labels like 'LOE1 LOE 1 — Authorize'.
nodes.languageNotes: Asserts the call sites, not the helper: the helper's unit test passed the whole time while four registers misrendered, because a unit test cannot see whether call sites actually use it.

nodes.name: cost-rate-gate.arch.test.ts
nodes.summary: Grep-based architecture test enforcing that costRate is FINANCE_READ data on every path out of the system — added after workbook exporters passed includeCost: true and wrote into spreadsheets the very field the staffing API withheld from callers without FINANCE_READ.
nodes.languageNotes: Strips comments before matching so the rule does not fire on the prose that explains it — an arch test that flags documentation teaches people to phrase around it.

nodes.name: brand-literals.arch.test.ts
nodes.summary: Architecture test asserting that migrated brand-surface files (layout, manifest, brand components, login, sidebar) never hardcode the COSMOS brand literal and instead resolve it via getBrand()/ProductProfile.
nodes.languageNotes: Source-scanning architecture test: reads the listed files at test time with readFileSync and regex-matches for the forbidden literal rather than importing them.

nodes.name: no-client-identity.arch.test.ts
nodes.summary: Public-repo identity gate that scans every git-tracked text file for forbidden client and vertical identity tokens, failing the build if any leak into the neutral open core.
nodes.languageNotes: The forbidden tokens are stored base64-encoded so the gate file itself never contains the literals it scans for, protecting it from identity scrubs and history rewrites.

nodes.name: board-visibility.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for visibleBoards covering shared (null-team) boards, multi-team membership, project-admin override, order preservation, and empty inputs.

nodes.name: board-visibility.ts
nodes.summary: Pure, synchronous rule deciding which of a project's boards a viewer sees: boards with a null teamId are project-wide, team boards require membership, and project admins see everything.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately a pure function rather than a database query so callers that already know the actor's teams can apply it without I/O, and tests need no database.

nodes.name: visibleBoards
nodes.summary: Filters a board list to those visible to a viewer: all boards for project admins, otherwise shared boards plus boards owned by any of the viewer's teams, preserving input order.

nodes.name: project-read-gate.arch.test.ts
nodes.summary: Architecture test scanning every route.ts under projects/[projectId] to assert no read is gated on a bare requireAccess without a project-visibility check, and that the high-traffic work-items route actually calls requireProjectRead.
nodes.languageNotes: Guards the rule rather than individual call sites: recursively walks the route tree at test time, and asserts the scan found a realistic file count so a directory move fails loudly instead of passing vacuously.

nodes.name: project-read-gates.test.ts
nodes.summary: Architecture test asserting no route under projects/[projectId] gates a read on an org-wide requirePermission(ctx, Permission.*_READ) bit, forcing the team-aware requireProjectRead pattern instead.

nodes.name: project-visibility-coverage.test.ts
nodes.summary: Capability-level guard over src/app and src/lib: any code enumerating or counting projects via Prisma must narrow the result to what the actor may see, or carry a SCOPING NOTE exemption directly beside the call.
nodes.languageNotes: Checks exemptions per occurrence with an asymmetric line window (15 before, 45 after) so a file-level note cannot silently absolve later calls; id-in hydration queries are excluded since they cannot widen visibility.

nodes.name: unnarrowedCalls
nodes.summary: Scans source text line by line for project enumeration calls and returns line numbers of any that are neither id-hydration, narrowed by a sanctioned helper nearby, nor exempted by an adjacent SCOPING NOTE.

nodes.name: date-only.arch.test.ts
nodes.summary: Architecture test asserting the time-tracker component never wraps a date-only entry value in new Date() (which shifts it a day in western timezones) and instead formats and groups via UTC-derived helpers like formatDateStable and dateOnlyKey.
nodes.languageNotes: A source-level check is used precisely because the bug is timezone-dependent and invisible to unit tests running in UTC.

nodes.name: not-voided.arch.test.ts
nodes.summary: Architecture test asserting every timeEntry Prisma query under src/app/api and src/lib filters out voided rows (or appears on a reasoned exemption list), preventing deleted entries' hours from billing against a contract.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes a self-check that the exemption list only names files that still exist, so a stale exemption cannot silently re-permit the bug under a recycled path.

nodes.name: vitest.config.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest configuration setting a jsdom environment with React plugin, the @ path alias to src, 30-second test and hook timeouts to tolerate ~390 test files contending on one Postgres, and include globs covering src plus cutover, dsop, and plugin scripts (including composed-plugin .mts daemon tests).
nodes.languageNotes: The 30s timeout is documented in-file as a deliberate trade-off: DB-backed specs that pass in isolation timed out intermittently at the 5s default under full-suite contention, and intermittent failures train developers to re-run rather than read.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to understand what Cosmos is: a multi-tenant project- and program-management platform (boards, OKRs, RAID logs, SAFe program increments) with a distinctive feedback-to-delivery automation pipeline, where user feedback is auto-triaged into backlogs and an autonomous 'Foreman' daemon can ship the work. AGENTS.md complements this with the contributor conventions that govern the codebase — SemVer rules, secret hygiene, and coding norms. Together they give you the vocabulary for everything that follows.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: Cosmos is a Next.js 16 App Router application, so the root layout is where every page begins: it generates brand-driven metadata, inlines skin CSS presets, and mounts global providers for branding, motion, and telemetry. Because Next.js routes by filesystem convention rather than imports, this file is deliberately thin — the real composition happens in the nested layouts you will see in Step 7. Note the multi-product 'brand' concept here: one codebase serves multiple branded deployments.
tour.languageLesson: In the Next.js App Router, layout.tsx files nest automatically by directory: the root layout wraps every route, and deeper layouts (like the dashboard shell) wrap only their subtree. This is convention-over-imports routing — the framework, not import statements, wires pages together.

tour.title: The Request Gatekeeper
tour.description: Before any page or API route runs, every request passes through src/proxy.ts — the Next.js middleware entry point. It applies security headers, enforces same-origin CSRF checks on mutating calls, and can flip the app into a cutover freeze. This is the platform's first line of defense and explains the security posture you will see repeated at every layer (this is a GovCon/CMMC-oriented product). The headers helper it delegates to centralizes the CSP and hardening policy.

tour.title: Data Model and Database Client
tour.description: The Prisma schema is the canonical data model: 126 models and 70 enums covering organizations and auth, projects and boards, OKRs, RAID logs, finance, CRM, feedback, and the Foreman delivery tables — it is the single best map of what the product actually does. Every query in the app flows through the singleton Prisma client in src/lib/db/client.ts, which with 515 inbound dependencies is the most depended-upon file in the entire codebase.
tour.languageLesson: Prisma schemas declare models and relations in a DSL; `prisma generate` produces a fully typed client, and `prisma migrate` emits versioned SQL migration files. The client is cached on globalThis in development so Next.js hot reloads do not exhaust database connections — a standard pattern for Prisma + Next.js.

tour.title: Auth, RBAC, and Audit
tour.description: This cluster is the platform's authorization backbone and ranks 2nd through 5th in fan-in across the graph. session.ts resolves the current user from the session cookie and builds a per-org auth context; permissions.ts defines every permission as a BigInt bit flag with per-role masks; check.ts computes a member's effective mask and asserts required permissions; and audit.ts persists a structured audit trail for nearly every mutation. Every API route in Step 6 leans on all four, so understanding them now makes the rest of the codebase legible.
tour.languageLesson: BigInt bit flags let TypeScript represent hundreds of permissions in a single integer: each permission is 1n << position, roles are OR-ed masks, and a check is just (mask & required) === required — constant-time authorization with no table lookups.

tour.title: API Route Conventions
tour.description: All server functionality is exposed as App Router REST routes under src/app/api/v1/orgs/[orgId]/..., so every URL is org-scoped by construction — the heart of multi-tenancy. api-helpers.ts (313 dependents) standardizes the pattern: JSON responders plus a centralized handleApiError that maps domain errors to 403/404/409 responses. The work-items and boards routes are representative examples: authenticate via Step 5's session, assert RBAC, query via Step 4's Prisma client, audit, respond. Once you have read one route, you can read all ~200 of them.

tour.title: Multi-Tenant Dashboard Shell
tour.description: On the page side, the (dashboard) route group's layout is the authenticated shell: it loads the current user, org memberships, and per-org enabled modules/plugins before rendering any child page. The [orgSlug] segment resolves which tenant you are in, and the project layout below it resolves the project by key — mirroring in the UI the same org-then-project scoping the API enforces in Step 6. This is where role- and module-based navigation gets composed.

tour.title: UI System and Client Data Layer
tour.description: Client components share a small, heavily reused toolkit. The cn() helper and the design-system primitives in src/components/ui (button.tsx alone has 142 dependents) come from the shadcn/@base-ui pattern. On the data side, json-fetcher.ts wraps fetch with typed errors for React Query, use-org-mutation.ts auto-invalidates org-scoped query keys after writes, and types/models.ts holds the client-side model definitions that mirror the Prisma schema from Step 4. These five files define the idioms used by essentially every feature component.
tour.languageLesson: React Query's cache is keyed by hierarchical query keys; scoping every key by orgId means a mutation can invalidate just that tenant's data. Throwing a typed FetchError from the fetcher (instead of returning it) is what lets React Query drive retries and error states uniformly.

tour.title: Boards and Work Items
tour.description: Now the core product surface. The Kanban board and Backlog view are two of the six board renderings over the same work-item data, and issues-view.tsx and card-detail-sheet.tsx are the highest fan-out feature components in the graph — the detail sheet alone composes 32 modules to edit a single work item (fields, comments, links, dependencies, activity). Notice how they consume the Step 8 idioms: json-fetcher hooks for reads, use-org-mutation for writes, and ui primitives throughout. Board choreography (Backlog → To-do → In progress → Review → Done) is also the state machine the Foreman daemon drives in Step 11.

tour.title: Feedback Portal to Backlog
tour.description: This is stage one of the README's headline pipeline. The in-app feedback portal lets any user file feature requests and bug reports; the org-scoped feedback API stores and manages them; and the remediate endpoint is where automation enters — an hourly GitHub Actions workflow POSTs to it, triggering Claude-powered triage that classifies feedback and delivers it into the target project's backlog from Step 9. Human capture, scheduled machine triage.

tour.title: AI Engine and the Foreman Daemon
tour.description: The AI subsystem in src/lib/ai powers both the in-app assistant and autonomous delivery. agent-loop.ts is the unified tool-use loop; tools.ts registers ~90 native tools spanning work items, OKRs, finance, and CRM; and tool-executor.ts parses the model's tool calls and dispatches them to domain executors — always through the same RBAC and audit layers from Step 5, so the AI has no privileged path. The autonomous-delivery runbook then documents Foreman, the host-side daemon that works the backlog: isolated branch per ticket, checks, an adversarial reviewer agent, then PR, auto-merge, signed release, and deploy — or a parked draft PR for risky changes.

tour.title: Containerization and Deployment
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the app as a multi-stage build — deps installs packages, build runs prisma generate and next build, and separate migrate and runtime stages run as a non-root user with only the Next.js standalone output. docker-compose.yml orchestrates the full in-boundary stack: pgvector Postgres with pgBackRest backups, TLS-bootstrapped MinIO object storage, a one-shot Prisma migration runner, and optional observability and OAuth-broker profiles. The Helm values file shows the same system deployed to Kubernetes with digest-pinned, hardened defaults for air-gapped and DoD postures.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds use multiple FROM statements so dev dependencies never reach production; a dedicated migrate stage lets orchestrators run schema migrations as a one-shot job before the app starts. Compose 'profiles' make optional service groups (observability, Nango) opt-in within one file.

tour.title: CI/CD, Security Gates, and Release
tour.description: The capstone: how code ships. ci.yml gates every push and PR with type-checks, lint, and unit plus DB-integration tests; security.yml runs the CMMC L2 / NIST 800-171 scanning gates; and release.yml builds signed multi-arch images to GHCR on v* tags — the same signed images the Foreman pipeline from Step 11 deploys and health-gates. package.json is the single source of truth for the running version (v2.x SemVer), tying the release automation back to the conventions you read in AGENTS.md at Step 1.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows trigger via 'on' (push, pull_request, schedule, tags); separating CI, security, and release into distinct workflows lets each run on its own trigger and permissions scope. Tag-triggered release jobs ('v*') are how SemVer tags become immutable, signed container artifacts.
